Title: anak krakatau shows renewed activity, alert raised to level III
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's Anak Krakatau volcano has shown renewed activity, recording at least 13 eruptions on Friday and prompting authorities to raise its alert status to Level III, the second-highest level in the country's four-tier volcanic alert system.
The Geological Agency said the alert was raised from Level II effective 9 pm local time on Friday, following an assessment of volcanic activity since early this month.
"Signs of increased activity on a low scale began to emerge in early October 2026," the agency said in its assessment dated Oct 9.
It noted however, that seismic monitoring had not indicated a significant overall increase in volcanic earthquakes.
Anak Krakatau, located in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, was downgraded to Level II on Sept 21 following a reduction in volcanic activity, after remaining at Level III since early September.
The latest activity follows a series of major eruptions in early September that sent volcanic ash into the atmosphere, forcing temporary airport closures.
The event disrupted 2,961 flights and affected about 341,000 passengers.
According to eruption reports published on the Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation Centre's (PVMBG) website, Friday's documented eruptions included one at 4.17pm that sent an ash column 250 metres above the summit, followed by another at 4.30pm with a 150-metre column.
Eleven further eruptions were recorded between 6.28spm and 9.20pm, although their ash columns could not be observed. PVMBG's full-day seismic monitoring recorded 26 eruption earthquakes.
Apart from Friday's 13 individually reported eruptions, Anak Krakatau recorded at least five others earlier this month — four on Oct 5 and one on Oct 8 — bringing the documented minimum to 18 since the beginning of October.
The Geological Agency said satellite monitoring detected sulphur dioxide emissions ranging from 71 to 237.5 tonnes per day between Sept 21 and Oct 9, while incandescence had been observed at the volcano since Oct 6.
Meanwhile, according to an advisory issued by Australia's Darwin Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre (VAAC), volcanic ash reached an altitude of about 1.8 kilometres above sea level at 10.50pm on Friday, drifting westward over the Sunda Strait towards the Indian Ocean at approximately nine kilometres per hour, before being forecast to dissipate within six to 12 hours.
The Geological Agency warned residents, visitors, and tourists of volcanic rocks, heavy ashfall, lava flows, and secondary eruptions, and prohibited all from entering a five-kilometre radius of the eruption centre and areas within one kilometre of two newly formed islands northwest and southeast of Anak Krakatau.
It also urged coastal communities in Banten and Lampung provinces to remain calm, avoid spreading unverified tsunami claims, and follow official safety instructions. — BERNAMA

Title: RM12.47mil in cryptocurrency stolen from man's digital wallet
Article:
IPOH: A 38-year-old man has suffered losses of RM12.47 million after his cryptocurrency assets were transferred from his digital wallet without his knowledge or authorisation.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the victim discovered the loss while he was in Teluk Intan about 1pm yesterday.
He said preliminary investigations found that the transactions involved the transfer of cryptocurrency assets through a blockchain network.
"Police are conducting further investigations to identify those involved and trace the transactions, with assistance from the Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department's Cryptocurrency Unit," he said in a statement.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating, which carries a jail term of between one and 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Alwi advised the public, particularly cryptocurrency and digital wallet users, to remain vigilant against phishing attempts and online scams.
He reminded users not to click on suspicious links or disclose their recovery phrases, private keys or passwords to anyone.
"Users are also advised to check their transaction records and connected applications regularly, and to keep savings wallets separate from those used for daily transactions.
"Anyone who suspects their account has been compromised should stop using the affected device, preserve digital evidence, contact the platform provider through official channels and lodge a police report," he said.
He also urged the public to strengthen their digital security measures to avoid falling victim to cybercrime.

Title: Malaysians welcome Budget aid, but seek long-term solutions to rising living costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians have welcomed measures in the 2027 Budget to ease financial pressures but called for longer-term solutions to rising living costs, employment challenges and education needs.
Full-time GrabFood rider Ahyar Amat, 35, said the measures would help ease the burden of rising living costs, particularly for private-sector employees and gig workers.
"We feel less burdened by the current economic situation, with costs continuing to rise. I think the measures are encouraging for Malaysians," he said.
However, he hoped the government would provide further support for gig workers, whose incomes were often unpredictable.
"Our income is not increasing; it is actually decreasing. We hope the government will do more for the gig economy, especially for riders," he said.
SJKC teacher Kweh Ci Yin said more financial support was needed to upgrade school infrastructure and facilities, particularly classrooms designed for 21st Century Learning.
​​​​​​​"As an SJKC teacher, I would like more government support to improve our infrastructure, especially to develop PAK-21 classrooms. We need financial assistance to upgrade our facilities," she said, adding that she was satisfied with the measures announced so far.
Fresh graduate Karthigeswary Mageswaran, 23, said financial assistance would help young Malaysians manage daily expenses, including transport and rent.
While welcoming cost-of-living assistance and measures for National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) borrowers, she said longer-term solutions were needed to provide greater financial stability.
"One-off assistance can help for a while, but we need to focus on the long term because the cost of living keeps rising," she said.
She also called for more jobs suited to graduates' qualifications, particularly in specialised fields such as biotechnology and microbiology, as well as higher starting salaries.
Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris (UPSI) student Nurul Syahzanani Khairudin, 18, said the RM200 early schooling assistance would help families with several school-going children.
"The RM200 assistance would help my brothers, as three of them are in primary and secondary school.
"There are many things my parents may not be able to afford, so the money could help them buy the things they still need," she said.
The responses reflected a shared call for the Budget to go beyond immediate financial relief and address longer-term concerns over income growth, employment opportunities, education and the rising cost of living.

Title: Brazil police rescue 13 children held hostage, assailant dead
Article:
RIO DE JANEIRO: Police in Brazil on Friday rescued 13 children who had been taken hostage at their kindergarten and killed the assailant who threatened to set fire to the building, officials said.
The incident took place in the southern city of Curitiba.
"We successfully neutralised this person and saved the 13 children, who were taken to be checked out and given care by first responders," the commander of the military police special forces unit in Parana state, Alexandre Lopes Dias, told reporters.
At least one of the children was wounded, he added.
The attacker arrived on a bicycle, jumped the gate at the municipal education centre for young children and barricaded himself in a room with the 13 kindergarteners.
He then spread a flammable substance in the room and held a lighter in his hand. He was carrying a knife and what was initially believed to be a firearm, but was later found to be fake.
"During the entire negotiation, he stayed with all the children around him and one on his lap," the police official said.
Talks lasted between two and a half and three hours. The children became agitated and the attacker started hitting them, Lopes Dias told reporters.
"Once we realised that the kids were becoming increasingly upset, and that the attacker started assaulting them physically, we opted for a tactical intervention to avoid a greater problem," he explained.
Images shown on local television stations revealed teachers and other school personnel ushering other children out of the facility.
Local media reported that several shots were fired and that they heard what sounded like flashbangs.
Police said the assailant had been identified and had schizophrenia. His motive was not immediately clear, nor was it clear whether he had ties to anyone at the kindergarten.
"The 13 children are alive and safe!" Curitiba Mayor Eduardo Pimentel wrote on Instagram.
"After anguishing and tense moments, this is the news we were all waiting for."
Brazil has experienced multiple attacks on schools in recent years. In April 2023, a man killed four children with an axe at a day care centre in Blumenau, also in southern Brazil.

Title: India deploys police, restricts transport ahead of major protests
Article:
New Delhi, Oct 10, 2026 (AFP) -
India deployed thousands of police in its capital and restricted transportation in and around Delhi ahead of mass demonstrations on Saturday demanding the resignation of the country's election chief over alleged voter-roll irregularities.
The protests, called by the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), are the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilisation following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter-roll revision.
Demonstrations erupted across the country after a newspaper investigation last month alleged misconduct by the Election Commission of India (ECI).
The ECI has rejected allegations of impropriety in the "special intensive revision", saying it was intended to remove duplicate and ineligible voters.
Opposition parties and critics say the exercise could disenfranchise voters to the benefit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Tens of thousands of police officers and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across the capital, with multiple layers of yellow metal barricades blocking roads leading to Jantar Mantar, the usual government-designated protest site.
Police have not authorised rallies at the site this weekend.
The protests, called by the CJP, are widely seen as a reprise of its mass mobilisation in July, which led to the education minister stepping down over an examination scandal.
This time, they are demanding ECI chief Gyanesh Kumar resign.
- 'Cannot detain the movement' -
The allegations are a fresh challenge for 76-year-old Modi during his third term in office.
Authorities have ordered the closure of dozens of metro stations, and cancelled several trains coming to New Delhi.
However, the Supreme Court on Friday said some trains must still run and that there should be no blanket closure of metro stations.
"The dictator would rather shut down the entire national capital and inconvenience millions of citizens than allow a peaceful protest at a designated protest site," CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke said on X.
"Imagine how many lives would be affected because of this shutdown by Modi."
The CJP, which emerged online as a satirical political movement in May, has accused authorities of intimidating its supporters ahead of the demonstration.
The party has said that "at least 10,000 people", including protesters travelling to Delhi by train, have been detained across the country.
Some people detained in the central state of Madhya Pradesh were taken to hotels, The Hindu newspaper reported.
Police have not responded to the party's broader allegations of mass detentions.
"You can detain the people – you cannot detain the movement," said Neha Bora, who has emerged as a leading face of the current protest.
The voter list overhaul, which began in 2025, has led to more than 133 million names being excluded from draft rolls.
The exclusions include duplicate entries and people found to have died.
The poll body said the exercise identifies fraudulently registered voters and aims to prevent "foreign illegal immigrants" from casting ballots.
Critics say the drive has disproportionately affected marginalised and minority communities.
Members of Modi's Hindu nationalist BJP have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India's electoral rolls.

Title: US says Chinese actions off Taiwan are 'deeply destabilising'
Article:
TAIPEI: China's maritime actions off Taiwan's east coast are "deeply destabilising" and only worsen tensions, the US State Department said, after Reuters reported the first known sighting of a Chinese militia boat in those waters in August.
China, which views Taiwan as its own territory, has stepped up activity off the island's east coast since June, with regular coast guard patrols.
Officials in Taiwan, which rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, say they believe China is practising for a possible maritime blockade using overlapping military, paramilitary and civilian assets.
Taipei regards the area off its east coast as critical to wartime supply routes from allies in the event of a blockade or conflict.
The United States remains concerned by China's activity east of Taiwan, a State Department spokesperson said, responding to a question about the sighting of the militia boat.
"China's actions are deeply destabilising," the spokesperson added.
"By asserting authorities around maritime areas that Taiwan has peacefully administered for over 70 years, China only exacerbates tensions and undermines the peaceful resolution of issues that it claims to seek."
The United States urges Beijing to cease its pressure on Taiwan and instead engage in "meaningful dialogue with Taiwan's democratically elected authorities", the spokesperson added.
China's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. China recognises no claims of sovereignty by Taiwan, including over the waters surrounding it.
The United States is Taiwan's most important international backer, though President Donald Trump has yet to approve a new US$14 billion arms sale package for the island.
Taiwan's Coast Guard said in a statement about the militia boat and its accompanying vessels that their activities were all located outside "restricted waters".
In a practice dating to the 1950s, China's maritime militia, more commonly seen around South China Sea flashpoints, consists of fishing vessels whose crews receive training and support to operate in disputed waters, often alongside coast guard ships.
In June, Britain, France, Germany and the United States all expressed concern over Chinese activities off Taiwan's east coast, citing threats to regional stability and freedom of navigation.

Title: Man with 10 previous criminal offences shot after police chase
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A man with 10 previous criminal offences was shot and injured after leading police on a chase from Petaling Jaya towards Sungai Buloh while driving dangerously and ramming other vehicles yesterday.
Petaling Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said the man, who is in his 30s, was driving a Proton Wira when police apprehended him.
He said police received a report on the incident around 6.42pm.
"The suspect drove aggressively and dangerously, ramming other vehicles before he was apprehended by police at the scene.
"He sustained injuries after being shot by police and is receiving treatment at Universiti Malaya Medical Centre (UMMC)," he said in a statement today.
Shamsudin said a policeman was also injured in the incident and had received treatment.
Checks revealed that the suspect had 10 previous police offences, comprising six drug-related cases and four criminal cases.
Police also found drugs and a toy weapon resembling a pistol in the vehicle. A urine test has yet to be conducted as the suspect is still receiving medical treatment.
Shamsudin said police were investigating why the suspect fled when officers attempted to stop him.
The case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of their duties, Section 279 for rash or dangerous driving and Section 307 for attempted murder.
Investigations are also being conducted under Section 36(1) of the Arms Act 1960 and Sections 39B and 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Shamsudin said an application for a remand order against the suspect was scheduled to be made at UMMC today.
Videos of the incident have since gone viral on social media, showing a foot chase and several police vehicles at the scene.
Those with information can contact the nearest police station or the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters operations room at 03-7966 2222 to assist in the investigation.

Title: Lorry driver who rammed into 11 vehicles tests positive for drugs
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A lorry driver who rammed into 11 vehicles at a traffic light junction in Alam Budiman, Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, yesterday tested positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine.
The
collision
, involving a 10-tonne lorry and 11 other vehicles at the traffic lights on Jalan Mokhtar Dahari, Section U10, left four people injured, including a 58-year-old man who sustained critical head injuries.
The 51-year-old lorry driver was arrested to assist in investigations after a urine test returned positive for both substances.
Shah Alam district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said the 4.20pm collision involved 12 vehicles, including the 10-tonne lorry.
Based on preliminary investigations, the driver claimed that his vehicle suffered brake failure while travelling downhill from Puncak Perdana towards Puncak Alam, causing him to lose control.
The lorry then crossed into the opposite lane and rammed into 11 vehicles stopped at the traffic lights.
Sarudin said a breathalyser test and a urine test were conducted on the driver, with the latter returning positive for both substances.
He said a 58-year-old man driving a Subaru XV suffered severe head injuries and was receiving treatment in the red zone at Hospital Al-Sultan Abdullah, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), Puncak Alam.
The victim's 53-year-old wife and 17-year-old grandson, who were also in the vehicle, were receiving treatment at the same hospital and were reported to be in stable condition.
Another victim, a 29-year-old Perodua Myvi driver, sustained bodily injuries and was also in stable condition.
The case is being investigated under Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Those with information can contact the investigating officer, Inspector Abdul Nasser Peping, at 012-286 3875.

Title: E-hailing, p-hailing workers welcome insurance cost relief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The RM160 million support package for e-hailing and p-hailing workers announced under the 2027 Budget, particularly vehicle insurance assistance, can ease operating costs and boost net income for drivers and riders facing rising premium rates.
Persatuan Rakan Grab Malaysia (PRGM), representing over 20,000 members nationwide, said in a statement that rising insurance premiums were among the earliest issues raised during engagement sessions with Grab Malaysia since its establishment last month.
"Insurance cost assistance under the 2027 Budget is a most welcome development and has the potential to offer meaningful relief to thousands of e-hailing driver partners nationwide," the statement said.
PRGM acknowledged Grab Malaysia's initiative to offer daily insurance payment options to ease drivers' financial pressure, but noted that this focused primarily on payment flexibility and did not fully address overall premium hikes.
The association also welcomed other components in the package, including increased minimum earnings rates, vehicle maintenance assistance, Social Security Organisation contributions, and initiatives to boost demand for e-hailing services.
However, PRGM urged that the implementation mechanism account for operating cost variations by location, service type, and driver needs to ensure benefits are distributed fairly.
The statement added that cooperation between the government and Grab Malaysia is essential to reducing operational costs and improving net income for drivers and riders.
PRGM said it will continue to bridge Grab partners, Grab Malaysia, and the government to ensure ground-level feedback and challenges faced by gig workers are addressed through constructive engagement.
The association expressed hope for stronger collaboration with Grab Malaysia, particularly on issues directly impacting earnings, operating costs, and the welfare of drivers and riders.
"For PRGM, the success of any policy lies not just in the allocated sum announced, but in how meaningfully the benefits are felt by drivers and delivery partners working daily to support their families," it said.

Title: Hannah Yeoh seeks lasting solution to homelessness in Kuala Lumpur
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has been directed to review data on homeless people in the city centre collected through enforcement operations over the past three years.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the review was aimed at identifying the best solutions to address homelessness in the city centre.
She also wants to seek input from non-governmental organisations (NGOs) working on the ground before bringing any proposed measures to the Cabinet.
"I do not want us to simply keep repeating enforcement operations against homeless people.
"I want us to improve the system so that those who need help do not keep returning to the streets," she said in a statement last night.
On Tuesday, Yeoh, who is also the Segambut member of parliament, joined the KL Strike operation in Kuala Lumpur, involving DBKL, the Social Welfare Department and other relevant agencies.
She acknowledged that homelessness could persist if adequate follow-up support was not provided after individuals were screened and referred to the relevant agencies.
"How long are we going to keep carrying out the same homeless outreach operations if they eventually return to the streets?
"I have seen the challenges on the ground myself. Screening facilities are limited, some people lack identification documents and require mental health treatment, while senior citizens and children need protection," she said.

Title: #NSTviral: Boy waves, train honks, hearts melt in Kempas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A simple wave from a boy to a passing Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) train in Kempas, Johor, warmed hearts online after the driver returned the greeting with a wave and a honk.
The moment, captured on video and shared on Threads by the boy's mother, user @_zrily,
showed her son waving at the passing train
before the driver responded.
Delighted by the gesture, she took to social media to thank the driver for making her son's day.
"Who was the man driving the train near Kempas at 6.30pm earlier? Thank you so much for making my child so happy today," she wrote.
The video has since garnered more than 92,000 views and 5,000 likes, drawing smiles from social media users.
The exchange even caught the attention of KTMB, which responded to the post through its official Threads account.
"Thank you for sharing this adorable moment. Your child's smile and happiness are our happiness too," it said.
The video also sparked a wave of nostalgia among social media users, many of whom recalled their childhood days of waving at passing trains.
Several reminisced about a time when trains were a familiar sight in their neighbourhoods and waving to locomotive drivers was a simple childhood pleasure.
Others were pleased to see the tradition continuing with a new generation of children.

Title: Batu Pahat tops API readings at 190, 32 locations unhealthy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Batu Pahat recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 190 as of 8am today, as worsening haze affected several areas in Johor and Negri Sembilan.
According to data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Larkin, Pasir Gudang, and Tangkak recorded an API of 185.
Seremban registered an API of 184, followed by Segamat at 181 and Nilai at 180.
As of 8am, 32 locations nationwide recorded unhealthy API readings, while 36 showed moderate air quality. No locations recorded good or hazardous air quality.
In the Klang Valley, at least nine locations, including Putrajaya, Cheras, and Shah Alam, recorded unhealthy API levels above 101.
The worsening conditions prompted authorities to implement precautionary measures, including school closures in severely affected areas.
The current haze episode is linked to forest and peatland fires in neighbouring Indonesia, where dry weather has accelerated the spread of fire and smoke across the region.
Malaysia and Indonesia are stepping up cooperation to tackle transboundary haze through hotspot monitoring, enforcement against open burning, and enhanced firefighting measures.
Both nations have also discussed potential cloud-seeding operations and resource-sharing, with Malaysia continuing to engage Indonesia and other Asean members on the recurring issue.
The haze remains a recurring regional environmental problem during prolonged dry spells, when smoke from Indonesian land fires drifts across national borders.
Malaysia continues to monitor air quality through APIMS, issue health advisories, and coordinate agency responses when API readings reach unhealthy levels.
The Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution, adopted in 2002, serves as the regional framework for member states to prevent, monitor, and mitigate land and forest fires.

Title: 'Loe appeared in my dreams three times; he wants to come home'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nearly two months after losing contact with her husband following the floods disaster in Nepal, Hani Othman remains hopeful that Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa will return to his family.
In a Facebook post today, Hani shared that her husband, better known as Loe, had appeared in her dreams three times, expressing his wish to return home.
"On this trip, he went to Nepal. He did not promise us that he would return safely because it was a leisure trip, not a dangerous climbing expedition.
"However, I know he wants to return. Three times he appeared in my dreams. He wants to return," she said.
Hani previously flew to Kathmandu on her own initiative to get direct updates on the search and rescue operations for her husband and his group, who have been untraceable for the past 46 days.
While there, Hani actively shared updates on efforts to locate her husband and other Malaysians.
She visited local hospitals for body identification processes and helped distribute aid to disaster victims alongside local non-governmental organisations.
Fakhrul Munir was reported missing after the four-wheel drive vehicle carrying his group on an expedition to Everest Base Camp via the Tibet route was believed to have been hit by severe floods and landslides in the Rasuwa valley.
Before going missing, Fakhrul Munir shared his personal views on social media on Aug 2 regarding the risks of extreme mountain climbing, referencing the Broad Peak tragedy and the 1996 Mount Everest disaster.
A total of 54 Malaysians were reported untraceable following the Aug 26 disaster.
In the same post, Hani uploaded a short video showing Fakhrul Munir briefing others on safety measures when encountering animals during an expedition in Phakding, Khumbu, Nepal.
"Knowing Loe, he prioritises safety. To him, life and safety are paramount. Not just his own life, but others as well, and he will fight to survive.
"He suffered from diarrhoea during his previous trip to Everest. He was capable of reaching the summit if he pushed for it, but he would have lost energy and risked dying on the descent.
"So he decided not to proceed even though he really wanted to reach the peak, because he had promised his family to return safely.
"But things turned out differently on this trip to Nepal," she said.

Title: Chief Judge heads Sarawak Governor's birthday honours list
Article:
KUCHING: Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi heads the list of recipients of state honours, awards and medals in conjunction with the 80th birthday celebration of Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar today.
She was conferred the Darjah Panglima Negara Bintang Sarawak (PNBS), which carries the title Datuk Seri.
Also receiving the PNBS were Dewan Negara president Datuk Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) pro-chancellor Datuk Abdul Wahab Aziz and ABM Fujiya Berhad chairman Datuk Tay Ah Ching @ Tay Chin Kin.
A total of 1,350 individuals received state honours in conjunction with the celebration.
Meanwhile, four recipients were conferred the Darjah Panglima Gemilang Bintang Kenyalang (PGBK), which carries the title Datuk.
The PGBK recipients are Court of Appeal Judge Dean Wayne Daly; Sarawak Deputy Minister of Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Datuk Sebastian Ting Chiew Yew; Sarawak State Legislative Assembly deputy speaker Datuk Idris Buang; and senior private secretary to the Sarawak Governor Datuk Seri Syed Hamzah Syed Paie.
Meanwhile, six individuals were conferred the Darjah Jasa Bakti Sarawak (DJBS), which carries the title Datu, while 23 individuals received the Darjah Panglima Setia Bintang Sarawak (PSBS), which carries the title Datuk.
The honours list also included two recipients of the Johan Bintang Sarawak (JBS), two of the Johan Bintang Kenyalang, one of the Johan Perkhidmatan Cemerlang, 16 of the Pingat Perkhidmatan Cemerlang, nine of the Pingat Perwira Negeri, 18 of the Pegawai Bintang Sarawak, 100 of the Pegawai Bintang Kenyalang and 204 of the Pingat Perkhidmatan Bakti.
A total of 71 individuals received the Ahli Bintang Sarawak, 241 were conferred the Ahli Bintang Kenyalang, 365 the Pingat Perkhidmatan Terpuji, while 284 received the Bentara Bintang Sarawak. — BERNAMA

Title: 2027 Budget: "Balance, discipline and pragmatic" [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget strikes a pragmatic balance between fiscal consolidation, economic growth and cost-of-living support, economists say.
However, its success will depend on whether public spending translates into higher household incomes, better jobs and stronger productivity.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid described the budget as pragmatic.
He said the government was seeking to maintain fiscal discipline while supporting the rakyat through targeted assistance and measures to ease financial pressures on households and businesses.
"We can see that cash transfers have been increased, alongside tax cuts for the M40 income group and small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
"Credit guarantees are also part of the budget measures to ensure SMEs continue to have access to financing," he told Business Times.
Universiti Teknologi Mara senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said the budget struck a reasonable balance between supporting economic growth, easing cost-of-living pressures and managing public finances.
He said targeted assistance and the government's commitment to reducing the fiscal deficit were among its key strengths, although the longer-term impact would depend on the effectiveness of public spending.
"The main weakness to watch is whether spending delivers sufficient productivity gains and higher-quality employment to support long-term growth.
"Ultimately, the success of the budget should be measured not only by its allocation of funds but also by whether it improves incomes, creates better jobs and strengthens the economy's capacity to withstand external shocks," he said.
DEFICIT REDUCTION MUST PRESERVE GROWTH
The federal fiscal deficit is projected to narrow to RM77.5 billion, or 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP), in 2027 from RM78.5 billion, or 3.6 per cent of GDP, in 2026, marking the sixth consecutive year of deficit reduction.
Total expenditure is projected to increase 3.6 per cent to RM459.8 billion, while development expenditure will rise 2.5 per cent to RM83 billion to support infrastructure, education, healthcare, flood mitigation and affordable housing.
Socio-Economic Research Centre executive director Lee Heng Guie said the government's continued commitment to fiscal discipline without sacrificing social and growth priorities was encouraging amid geopolitical tensions and global economic uncertainty.
He said the budget sought to provide immediate relief while advancing medium-term strategies to strengthen structural competitiveness, accelerate digital adoption and support sustainable economic growth.
However, Lee said Malaysia needed to broaden its revenue base and rationalise operating expenditure to sustain fiscal consolidation while preserving resources for productive investments.
Federal revenue is projected to grow 4.7 per cent to RM380.8 billion in 2027, while the tax-to-GDP ratio averaged 12.1 per cent in 2020-2027, compared with 13.8 per cent in 2010-2019.
Lee said the declining ratio highlighted the need to strengthen revenue collection, adding that the reintroduction of the goods and services tax was worth considering.
DEBT BURDEN CALLS FOR STRONGER REVENUE
Idham said narrowing the fiscal deficit and moderating new borrowing represented progress but would not necessarily lead to a rapid reduction in the overall debt stock as existing borrowings continued to incur interest and require servicing.
He said the government needed to sustain revenue growth, improve spending efficiency and ensure new borrowing financed productive investments capable of generating long-term economic returns.
"Equally important is maintaining a credible fiscal consolidation path without undermining essential social protection or development spending.
"The objective should be to reduce the debt burden relative to the economy while preserving sufficient fiscal space to respond to future economic shocks," Idham said.
PRODUCTIVITY AND JOBS KEY TO LONG-TERM GAINS
Idham said the government should strengthen Malaysia's competitiveness through three priorities: raising productivity and investment quality, reforming the labour market and improving public spending efficiency.
He said the government should accelerate automation, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and research and development, particularly among SMEs, to help businesses move into higher-value activities.
The labour market and skills ecosystem should also be better aligned with industry needs through technical and vocational education and training, higher education and reskilling programmes, while encouraging better wages and more high-skilled jobs.
He added that outcome-based budgeting, better coordination of government programmes and regular evaluations of incentives were needed to ensure public spending generated measurable gains in investment, employment and productivity.
"These reforms would help Malaysia compete on capabilities and innovation rather than cost alone, while supporting more sustainable and inclusive long-term growth," he said.
Meanwhile, Malaysia's economic growth is projected at between 4.2 and 5.2 per cent in 2027, compared with an estimated 4.8 to 5.3 per cent in 2026, as technology exports and investment activity moderate.
Lee cautioned that household spending remained constrained by rising living costs, food and services inflation, and elevated debt.
He said the government needed to ensure economic growth translated into broader improvements in purchasing power, as reliance on cash assistance and fuel subsidies highlighted persistent financial pressures on households.
"While overall private consumption might look stable, the underlying growth is narrow and a distinct absence of a broad-based consumption acceleration.
This indicates that consumers are not increasing their spending across retail, dining, or entertainment," he said.

Title: Saudi-led coalition says destroyed more than 100 Houthi targets
Article:
RIYADH (Saudi Arabia): The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said today it destroyed more than 100 military targets in a "large-scale operation" against the Iran-backed group.
The conflict between the Houthis and Yemen's internationally recognised government — which Saudi Arabia supports — reignited in July, and has since spilled over into the neighbouring kingdom.
In addition to seizing territory along the Red Sea coast in Yemen, the Houthis have attacked transport hubs, oil facilities and other civilian targets in the world's largest crude exporter with drones and missiles.
"We are carrying out a large-scale operation targeting the personnel and capabilities of the Houthi terrorist militia," Turki al-Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi coalition, wrote on X.
"We destroyed 136 military targets in areas controlled by the Houthi terrorist militia," he said in a separate post.
The Houthi's Almasirah TV channel reported that Saudi missiles targeted areas in the northwestern Yemeni governorate of Saada. — AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump appoints 'devoted fan' Katie Zacharia as press secretary
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Friday announced the appointment of conservative commentator Katie Zacharia as his new White House press secretary, praising her as a loyal supporter.
"She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning," Trump posted on his Truth Social platform.
"She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA!" he added, referring to his Make America Great Again movement.
Zacharia, a lawyer and communications adviser to Trump's media company, will succeed Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down in August after becoming one of the most prominent public faces of his second administration.
Trump praised his new spokeswoman's credentials, including her work for his presidential campaigns, and said he was confident she would enjoy a good relationship with the White House press corps.
Zacharia thanked Trump in a post on X for the "distinguished privilege of serving as White House Press Secretary".
Trump's "confidence is a true privilege, and his leadership is a blessing to this country," she wrote.
"The work ahead is to continue delivering strong results for our Country and communicating to the American people the major wins that this Administration is making every single day."
Zacharia currently serves as a senior communications adviser to Trump Media and Technology Group, which operates the president's Truth Social platform.
Trump described her work at his company as "outstanding".
A frequent commentator on conservative television networks, including Fox News and Newsmax, Zacharia previously served a brief stint as a spokeswoman for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees US immigration enforcement.
High-profile role
She joined the department under then-secretary Kristi Noem earlier this year but left after about two months, according to her LinkedIn profile.
Zacharia, who lives in California, has also worked with Fix California, a conservative advocacy group founded by Richard Grenell, a longtime Trump ally and one of his special presidential envoys.
According to CNBC, she serves as general counsel for the organisation, which seeks to advance conservative political causes in the Democratic-leaning state.
A graduate of Pepperdine University's law school, Zacharia began her career in Republican politics, working as an intern for the Republican National Committee in 2006, CNN reported.
Trump sought advice from several allies and advisers, including Leavitt, before deciding to offer Zacharia the position, according to CNN.
Her appointment fills one of the White House's most visible positions, with the press secretary responsible for briefing journalists, fielding questions about administration policies and serving as a chief public defender of the president.
Leavitt, who took up the position when Trump returned to power in January 2025, became the youngest White House press secretary in US history at 27.
A staunch Trump loyalist who previously served as press secretary for his 2024 presidential campaign, she left the administration in late August following the birth of her second child.
Fox News announced this week that Leavitt would join the conservative network as an on-air contributor beginning in November.
Trump praised his outgoing spokeswoman, saying she had done a "fantastic job" in the role.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Protests in New York as Trump administration defends ICE shooting
Article:
NEW YORK: Protesters gathered in New York on Friday after Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers shot a Dominican man in an incident that has provoked a showdown between the city's Democratic mayor and the Trump administration.
Oscar Bergal, 28, was wounded in the neck during an ICE operation in the Bronx on Thursday, while a five-year-old child who was in his car at the time was physically unharmed.
The shooting drew swift criticism from Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who wrote "Abolish ICE" on X — a common refrain among the political left opposed to Republican President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown.
US Homeland Security chief Markwayne Mullin lashed out in response, telling reporters that Mamdani's words were "dangerous and incite hostility".
"Mayor, if you abolish ICE, who's going to take criminals off the streets of your own town?" Mullin said. "Who's going to take the murderers and the thieves and the gangbangers?"
An AFP journalist saw hundreds of protesters stretching across several blocks in Manhattan on Friday, chanting "No hate, no fear, immigrants are welcome here" and "No ICE".
New York, a Democratic stronghold, is one of several US cities that bar their police forces from assisting with federal immigration enforcement.
Mamdani said on Thursday that he was seeking to speak with Trump and would demand that immigration agents be withdrawn from the city.
The incident could test the surprisingly warm relationship between the two leaders.
Video of the shooting, shared by US media on Friday, shows what appears to be a plainclothes federal agent rushing towards a silver car with a gun drawn.
The vehicle briefly reverses as the agent punches the driver-side window, before a second plainclothes officer draws a gun.
He points the weapon at the driver as the car pulls away off screen, appearing to collide with the side of a passing vehicle.
[[nid:1552133]]
High-profile shootings
Mullin said Bergal had an extensive criminal history and was trying to evade arrest.
"He came to this country legally a few years ago, and ever since he's come in, he's committed crime and crime after crime," the Homeland Security secretary said.
Mullin said ICE officers did not know there was a child in the car when they opened fire.
Marcos Charles, a senior ICE official, told reporters that Bergal had "refused lawful orders to exit his vehicle".
"He then accelerated his vehicle, smashing into two of our government ICE vehicles, and then weaponised his vehicle and proceeded to accelerate, going towards other officers," Charles said.
"Our officers, using their training, and believing that their life and the lives of their partners and general public were in danger, used their training and fired weapons," he said.
ICE agents, who often wear civilian clothing and cover their faces, have been involved in several high-profile shootings this year.
Ruben Ray Martinez, 23, was shot by ICE in March 2025 in what the Texas Tribune said was the first known killing of an American by immigration agents during Trump's second term.
More recently, a Mexican man, Lorenzo Salgado, died in July after being shot by an ICE officer in Houston, Texas.
Two Americans — Renee Good and Alex Pretti — were shot and killed by federal immigration agents in separate incidents in Minnesota during a crackdown on undocumented migrants in the northern state earlier this year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Brazil prosecutors sue Shell for US$108mil over deadly 2024 floods
Article:
BRASILIA: Brazilian prosecutors on Friday filed an unprecedented lawsuit against oil giant Shell's subsidiary in the country, demanding US$108 million in compensation over deadly 2024 floods.
Torrential rains sparked historic flooding in southern Brazil in April and May of that year, leaving nearly 200 people dead, 500,000 more displaced and causing massive damage.
According to the lawsuit, Shell's liability should match its contribution to global warming, estimated at two per cent of historical global greenhouse gas emissions.
"This civil suit is aimed at holding the defendant company accountable, in terms of its environmental and climate-related responsibilities, for collective material and moral damages stemming from the extreme weather event that hit Rio Grande do Sul state," public prosecutors said, according to court documents seen by AFP.
They said the British energy giant should be held responsible because of its past and current greenhouse gas emissions associated with the exploration, production and sale of fossil fuels.
The US$108 million in compensation covers both material and moral damages.
The filing of a new climate-related lawsuit by Brazilian prosecutors, in conjunction with Instituto Preservar, a Brazilian NGO, marks a new phase in the global legal battle against oil giants.
"This is the first time a national public prosecutor is suing an oil major for a climate disaster," Maria Antonia Tigre, director of global climate litigation at the Sabin Center for Climate Change Law, told AFP.
Shell is already being sued in the United Kingdom by victims of a typhoon in the Philippines.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump takes suit against Hillary Clinton over 2016 election to Supreme Court
Article:
NEW YORK: President Donald Trump asked the US Supreme Court on Friday to revive his dismissed lawsuit against his 2016 Democratic rival Hillary Clinton, accusing her, former FBI Director James Comey and others of conspiring to rig that year's election by linking his campaign to Russia.
The Republican president filed his appeal after a federal judge threw out the case and imposed nearly US$1 million in sanctions against Trump and one of his lawyers for bringing a "frivolous" suit. A US appeals court subsequently upheld the dismissal and sanctions.
In 2022, after losing the 2020 election and leaving office, Trump sued Clinton, Comey, former British intelligence officer Christopher Steele, the Democratic National Committee and numerous others in a lengthy complaint filed in federal court in Florida.
Trump, who has a history of suing adversaries, alleged that in the lead-up to the 2016 election, Clinton conspired with allies to discredit him with a "false narrative" that he and his campaign colluded with Russia.
The lengthy suit alleged "racketeering" and a "conspiracy to commit injurious falsehood", among other claims.
Trump defeated Clinton in that election, despite losing the national popular vote, and served his first term in office from 2017 to 2021.
US government officials have accused Russia of meddling in the 2016 election, and an investigation led by former FBI chief Robert Mueller documented extensive contacts between the Trump campaign and Russian operatives who sought to influence the election in his favour. Trump has called the idea of Russian interference a "hoax".
Since losing to Democrat Joe Biden in 2020, Trump has made false claims of widespread voting fraud in that year's election. Trump regained the presidency by defeating Democrat Kamala Harris in 2024 and has continued to make those false claims.
'Political manifesto'
US District Judge Donald Middlebrooks dismissed Trump's lawsuit against Clinton, citing numerous inadequacies, including that Trump had waited too long to bring some of the claims. The judge likened Trump's lawsuit to a "two-hundred-page political manifesto outlining his grievances against those that have opposed him".
Middlebrooks later ordered Trump and his lead attorney in the case, Alina Habba, to pay nearly US$1 million in fees and costs, imposing the sanctions for bringing a case that the judge said was intended "to dishonestly advance a political narrative". The judge also faulted Trump and his lawyers for a "continuing pattern of misuse of the courts".
Middlebrooks found that the lawsuit used abusive litigation tactics, contained "knowingly false" factual allegations and asserted "frivolous" legal theories.
The Atlanta-based 11th US Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the judge's rulings in 2025, including the sanctions.
"Many of Trump's and Habba's legal arguments were indeed frivolous," the 11th Circuit stated.
In court papers, lawyers for Trump and Habba said the lower courts' decisions were having a "profound impact on the presidency, and the nation as a whole".
Mueller, serving as a special counsel appointed by the Justice Department, issued a 2019 report on his investigation.
The report stated that Russia "interfered in the 2016 presidential election in sweeping and systematic fashion", but also stated that "the investigation did not establish that members of the Trump campaign conspired or coordinated with the Russian government in its election interference activities".
Mueller said in his report that he found "numerous links" and that the Trump campaign "expected it would benefit" from Russia's effort to tilt the ballot in Trump's favour.
Trump's then-Attorney General William Barr appointed a different special counsel, John Durham, in 2019 to investigate potential missteps by the FBI.
In a 2023 report, Durham concluded that the FBI lacked "actual evidence" to investigate Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and relied too heavily on tips provided by Trump's political opponents to fuel the probe.
Trump's Justice Department last year indicted Comey, one of several adversaries of the president to face criminal charges, accusing him of making false statements and obstructing Congress after he was accused of lying about authorising leaks to the news media.
A federal judge subsequently dismissed the indictment, finding that the prosecutor Trump had handpicked to prosecute Comey was unlawfully appointed.
Steele, working for an opposition research firm hired by a law firm on behalf of the Clinton campaign and the Democratic National Committee, produced a dossier alleging ties between Trump's campaign and Russia, as well as other salacious accusations, all of which Trump denied.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Outrage over plan to livestream US military firing squad execution
Article:
WASHINGTON: Condemnation of US plans for a public execution by military firing squad escalated on Friday, as Vice President JD Vance cast doubt on whether it would be livestreamed as proposed and insisted he would not watch if it was.
Nidal Hasan's execution — scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 — is set to be the first by US military firing squad since 1945.
Asked about the planned livestream, Vance told journalists he did not "know that that's actually going to happen".
"This is a guy who committed, in my view, the worst terrorist attack on American soil outside of 9/11," Vance said, but added that if the execution was broadcast live, "I'm not going to be watching it".
Representative Austin Scott of President Donald Trump's Republican Party said he supported executing Hasan but that "livestreaming executions is what jihadists do. America is better than that".
Senator Mark Kelly, a Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, said Hasan should "face justice" but that public executions were "the kind of thing Iran and the Taliban do. Is this who we want to be associated with?"
A Pentagon official told AFP on Thursday that the execution would be streamed live, after US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said "we'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public".
But Trump on Friday contradicted Hegseth's confirmation and said no decision had yet been made on whether to publicly broadcast the execution, which he supports.
"They are making a determination about that, but he will be killed," Trump said. "I really don't care how he goes, as long as he goes."
Tech firms YouTube, Meta and X did not immediately respond to requests for comment on whether they would allow the execution to be streamed on their platforms.
TikTok directed AFP to its policy banning depictions of "graphic incidents and violence", including "the shooting of an individual".
The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights condemned the move, saying in a message sent to AFP on Friday that "the livestreaming of an execution is tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture".
Archbishop Paul Coakley, president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops, said it was a "barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered".
'Compound the cruelty'
Hegseth said it would be the military's first firing squad execution since World War II.
"People need to understand that...there's serious consequence for these types of things," Hegseth said in a video shared on Thursday on official Pentagon X accounts.
The last US military execution was carried out in 1961, when John Bennett was hanged for rape and attempted murder.
The Death Penalty Information Center says 135 troops have been executed by the US military since 1916.
According to rights group Amnesty International, at least 17 public executions are known to have been carried out in 2025 — six in Afghanistan and 11 in Iran.
Amnesty's Justin Mazzola said on Friday that the death penalty was "a violation of human rights" and that streaming Hasan's execution "would only compound the cruelty".
Twelve of the 13 people Hasan killed and 30 of those he wounded were soldiers. He was shot by a civilian police officer who responded to the attack and is paralysed from the waist down.
Hasan chose to conduct his own defence during the trial but called no witnesses, gave no testimony and made no attempt to deny the charges.
He was sentenced to death by a military jury in 2013.
Court-appointed defence attorneys expressed concern that he was seeking execution.
The court that convicted Hasan was told he opposed the US military's occupations of Iraq and Afghanistan and had spoken online with an alleged Al-Qaeda figure, radical cleric Anwar al-Awlaki, an American citizen who was subsequently killed in a US drone strike in Yemen.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two students murdered, drama at Subang Airport [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The deaths of two students in separate incidents in Johor and Pahang were among the major crime cases reported by the New Straits Times this week.
In Yong Peng, 16-year-old student Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal was found dead at her school on Oct 3, while in Kuantan, a 19-year-old student, Elisa Jonova Masilamani, was found dead at a house on Oct 6 following an alleged argument with her boyfriend.
Below are some of the crimes reported this week.
FORM FOUR STUDENT FOUND DEAD AT JOHOR SCHOOL
Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16, was
found dead
at a secondary school in Yong Peng, Batu Pahat, on Oct 3.
Her grandmother found her covered in blood at the school's hall after realising that she had not returned home by about 5.30pm.
Police arrested three 16-year-old boys on the same day, with one remanded for six days until Oct 9.
Federal police Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said a post-mortem confirmed that Irene died from
blunt force trauma
to the head.
The case is being investigated for murder.
19-YEAR-OLD STUDENT STRANGLED TO DEATH IN KUANTAN
In Kuantan, Elisa Jonova Masilamani, a 19-year-old student
was found dead
at a house in Air Putih on Oct 6 following an argument with her boyfriend.
The boyfriend, also 19, contacted the police.
Police were immediately dispatched to the rented house along Jalan Air Putih 2 where they found Elisa Jonova lying unconscious on a bed inside a rented room on the ground floor.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the boyfriend was believed to be unhappy that the victim had met another man.
A post-mortem confirmed that Elisa Jonova died from strangulation.
The suspect has been remanded for seven days until Oct 12, with the case being investigated for murder.
DRAMA AT SUBANG AIRPORT AS FOUR NABBED
Enforcement teams swooped on a private jet at a
Subang Airport hangar
on Wednesday where they arrested four people moments before the aircraft was due to take off for Manila.
This was a follow-up operation as investigations widened into the recent case where Laos authorities uncovered an attempt to smuggle 521kg of crystal methamphetamine.
Among the  four who were arrested on Wednesday was a Malaysian pilot.
The operator of the private jet, CGT Asia Limited, has
denied any wrongdoing
after one of its aircraft was linked to an attempted trafficking of 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from Laos to the Philippines.
The company also confirmed that its director and three crew members, who were detained at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang on Wednesdayh  were released the same day after giving their statements to the Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID).
It was reported that they were preparing to take off when enforcement personnel moved in. It was learnt the aircraft was configured for medical evacuation operations and equipped with medical equipment.
The flight was understood to have been scheduled to fly to Manila to pick up a patient before transporting the patient to Japan.
This was believed to be a follow-up operation to the incident on Oct 1 when a private jet that left Subang for Laos later became the focus of a major drug investigation after authorities seized 521kg of crystal methamphetamine at the Luang Prabang International Airport.
Police later confirmed that the co-pilot on that flight was a Malaysian. He was among 13 people arrested in Laos.
POLICEMEN DENY TOUTING CLAIMS IN MCBA CHIEF CASE
The two Special Branch policemen allegedly assaulted by Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain at KLIA Terminal 1 on Sept 28
broke their silence
on Wednesday when they denied claims that they were acting as touts or involved in "counter setting".
Speaking through their lawyers, Lance Corporals Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman and Mohammad Faiz Muhamad, said they were carrying out official duties when the alleged incident occurred.
Their lawyers said any allegation that the policemen were acting as touts or involved in counter setting should be supported by evidence and should not be used to divert attention from the alleged assault.
The two were allegedly physically assaulted by Shuhaily in a public area, causing injuries and affecting their dignity as civil servants.
Police, meanwhile, said, they have recorded statements from 25 witnesses and obtained CCTV footage and a medical report.
The incident came to light after a video showing Shuhaily berating two men went viral, with one of them appearing to have been grabbed forcefully by the ears.
Shuhaily later said he was prepared to be investigated over the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: COURT WATCH: Murder charges, Zara Qairina inquest and major legal challenges [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An e-hailing driver has pleaded not guilty to three charges over a crash that killed a 22-year-old Maldivian student and injured another passenger, including driving under the influence of methamphetamine.
The case leads this week's Court Watch, alongside murder charges against two teenagers over the death of their junior, fresh developments in the Zara Qairina inquest, and several significant legal challenges.
E-hailing driver charged over crash that killed student, injured another
Five days after a crash claimed the life of a 22-year-old Maldivian student, an e-hailing driver was brought before the Shah Alam Magistrate's Court to face three charges linked to the accident, including causing death while driving under the influence of methamphetamine.
Muhamad Syafiq Ibrahim, 37, pleaded not guilty to a charge of driving a Perodua Ativa under the influence of methamphetamine, resulting in the death of Aamina Imeely Nazim, a private university student.
He also claimed trial to a second charge of driving the same vehicle under the influence of the drug, causing injuries to another 22-year-old Maldivian passenger, Aishath Sara Nizam.
Syafiq further pleaded not guilty to a third charge of driving without due care and attention, resulting in a collision with another vehicle and causing injuries to Aishath.
Aamina and Aishath were passengers in Syafiq's e-hailing vehicle.
The offences were allegedly committed at 8.40pm on Oct 4 along the Damansara-Puchong Highway, near the Puchong Selatan toll plaza, heading towards Puchong.
Police said the crash occurred when Syafiq's Ativa crashed into another car while approaching the toll plaza's RFID lane.
The impact caused the Ativa to spin before overturning.
Below are some of the other major court cases this week.
TWO TEENAGERS CHARGED WITH THE MURDER OF THEIR JUNIOR
In Kuala Pilah, two 16-year-old boys were
charged with murdering
their 14-year-old junior at a sports school hostel last month.
They were charged with murdering Muhammad Idlan Fareeq Shahril between 7.30pm and 8.50pm on Sept 25.
The proceedings, led by Negri Sembilan prosecution director Engku Ahmad Rashdi Engku Abdillah, were conducted in camera as both accused are juveniles.
Lawyer Datuk Hanif Hassan, who represented both teenagers, said the court had fixed Dec 7 for the submission of pathology, chemistry and forensic reports.
He said the defence had applied for both teenagers to be sent to a correctional centre pending the next court date to allow counselling by the Social Welfare Department.
CORONER'S COURT VISITS ZARA QAIRINA'S SCHOOL AGAIN
From the courtroom to SMKA Tun Datu Mustapha, the Coroner's Court returned to the school in Papar for a second site visit as
part of the inquest
into the death of 13-year-old Zara Qairina Mahathir.
The latest visit on Oct 5 lasted nearly four hours, with coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan, deputy public prosecutors and legal representatives of interested parties inspecting classrooms, the design and technology room, hostel dormitories and toilets.
Teachers and students familiar with the school also accompanied the group and helped clarify locations, layout and physical conditions referred to during the inquest.
The first site visit was conducted on Sept 11 last year.
Zara Qairina was found unconscious near a drain at her school hostel about 4am on July 16 last year and was pronounced dead the following day at Queen Elizabeth Hospital.
This week, Zara Qairina's half-sister, Malianah Mahathir, 25, and mother, Noraidah Lamat, 46, testified as the 81st and 82nd witnesses respectively.
UNDANGS WITHDRAW JUDICIAL REVIEW AFTER MB SIGNS PROCLAMATION
A legal challenge by the
Undang Yang Empat
came to an end after Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim signed the proclamation they had sought to compel him to sign.
The four Undangs had filed a judicial review application seeking an order requiring Ismail to sign the proclamation concerning the removal of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
However, Ismail signed the proclamation on Aug 3, before the court could hear the substantive challenge.
Lawyer Mohd Khairul Azam Aziz told High Court judge Norliza Othman that the application had become academic.
Norliza allowed the withdrawal without liberty for the applicants to file afresh and ordered them to pay RM40,000 in costs to four proposed interveners.
The four Undangs are Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, Datuk Muhammed Abdullah and Datuk Abd Rahim Yasin.
BAR FAILS TO CHALLENGE TERRIRUDIN'S JAC APPOINTMENT
The Malaysian Bar failed in its
bid to challenge
the appointment of Federal Court judge Tan Sri Ahmad Terrirudin Mohd Salleh to the Judicial Appointments Commission (JAC).
High Court judge Norliza Othman dismissed the Bar's application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings, ruling that the proposed challenge was not legally arguable.
She said Section 5(1)(e) of the Judicial Appointments Commission Act 2009 was clear in requiring the appointee to be a serving Federal Court judge and the appointment to be made by the prime minister.
The court found that both requirements were met in Ahmad Terrirudin's appointment.
The Bar had sought a certiorari order to quash Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's decision to appoint Ahmad Terrirudin as a member of the JAC.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mexican court finds three men guilty of 2024 killing of Australian, US surfers
Article:
MEXICO CITY: A Mexican judge on Friday found three men guilty of the 2024 murders of two Australian brothers and their American friend during a surf trip to the state of Baja California, a court source told Reuters.
Jesus Gerardo Garcia, known as "El Kekas", and the co-defendants identified simply as Irineo Francisco "N" and Angel Jesus "N", were found guilty of aggravated homicide, violent robbery and vehicle theft by a Baja California court.
The prosecution had sought sentences of up to 150 years for the suspects. According to the same source at the state court, the sentence will be announced on Oct 16.
Brothers Callum, 33, and Jake Robinson, 30, and American Jack Carter Rhoad, 30, were camping and surfing near Punta San Jose, about 80km south of Ensenada, when they were reported missing in late April 2024.
After a days-long search, aided by the FBI, their bodies were found on May 3 at the bottom of a well. The victims were each found with gunshot wounds to the head, authorities said.
Prosecutors said the accused had attempted to carjack the tourists, who were shot when they tried to resist. Their truck was later found burned nearby.
Martin and Debra Robinson, the Robinsons' parents, travelled from their hometown of Perth to attend the four-week trial. Rhoad's widowed fiancée, Natalie Weirtz, spoke via video call from the United States.
In November 2025, Gisell Silva, Garcia's then-girlfriend, was sentenced to 20 years in prison for her involvement in the case. The woman, who was 23 at the time, was arrested a few days after the victims' bodies were found.
While the Ensenada area is considered relatively safe, Baja California ranks among Mexico's most violent states. Following the killings, the US State Department urged Americans to reconsider travel to the state because of crime and kidnapping risks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Boarded windows and evacuations as major hurricane nears US Gulf coast
Article:
NEW MEXICO: Residents of coastal towns in Florida and Alabama boarded up windows and filled sandbags on Friday as Hurricane Isaias bore down on the US Gulf Coast, bringing life-threatening storm surges and winds of 185 kph.
Tens of thousands of people in Florida's Panhandle and along Alabama's Gulf Coast faced mandatory evacuation orders. Local television stations showed roads packed with vehicles heading north, away from the water.
The Category 3 Isaias, the first hurricane of an unusually quiet season for the United States, was expected to make landfall between Mobile, Alabama, and Grayton Beach in the Florida Panhandle on Friday evening, according to the National Hurricane Centre.
The 145-kilometre stretch of coast is known for its brilliant white sand beaches, with some areas packed with holiday homes next to small coastal towns such as Destin, Florida.
"If you've been asked to evacuate, get out now, conditions are only going to deteriorate," NHC Director Michael Brennan told Fox Weather on Friday. "That surge is going to come in after dark, that's not a place you are going to want to be in."
Scientists say human-caused climate change has warmed the Gulf of Mexico, possibly intensifying hurricanes such as Isaias.
[[nid:1552149]]
The storm was expected to bring sustained winds capable of causing extensive structural damage to beach houses, although modern homes built to strict coastal codes might remain standing. Storm surges of up to 2.7m were forecast around the Alabama-Florida border.
President Donald Trump cancelled a planned trip to Alabama on Saturday for the Georgia versus Alabama college football game, as the hurricane was expected to affect Tuscaloosa, the city where the match was due to be played.
Up to 38 cm of rain was expected in localised areas of the Florida Panhandle and the Big Bend area.
Oil companies had evacuated personnel from 129 oil and gas production platforms, representing 35 per cent of the 371 staffed platforms in the Gulf of Mexico.
Hurricane-force winds were expected as far as 100 miles inland in southern Alabama, possibly triggering tornadoes. Between 2 and 5 inches (5 to 13 cm) of rain were expected across the US Southeast, as far north as the southern Appalachian Mountains and coastal areas of the Carolinas.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 7.7-magnitude quake rocks Panama, triggers tsunami warning
Article:
PENONOME: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake rocked Panama on Friday, causing panic in the high-rise capital and bringing down buildings in the centre of the country, but there were no immediate reports of casualties.
The shallow tremor was felt across the Central American nation of around 4.5 million people, according to the National Civil Protection System, and lasted about a minute.
In Panama City, about 200km from the epicentre, people rushed to evacuate skyscrapers in scenes of panic.
A video widely shared on social media, which AFP could not verify, showed water spilling from a pool at the top of a building more than 20 storeys tall.
Another showed a bridge over the Panama Canal shaking violently but remaining upright as vehicles travelled across it.
"It was horrible, like nothing we ever experienced. My daughter was trapped in school. Thank God we are okay," Juana Alveo, a 38-year-old cashier at a store in the central city of Penonome, told AFP.
The US Geological Survey said the quake struck at 1756 GMT, with an epicentre 10km from the small town of Pitaloza Arriba in south-central Panama.
"I'm in shock right now and haven't been able to contact my family," Luis Poveda, a factory worker in Santiago de Veraguas, another city in central Panama, told AFP.
[[nid:1552125]]
The quake triggered a tsunami warning for Panama and warnings of smaller but dangerous waves along the coasts of other countries in Latin America and the South Pacific.
But the Panama Canal Authority said shipping through the channel, which connects the Pacific and Atlantic oceans, was unaffected and operating "as normal".
The damage appeared to be concentrated in the central regions of Herrera, Azuero, Veraguas and Los Santos.
"We all ran out of the building, the power lines were swaying, and everyone was outside," Arnulfo Santos, a worker at a flour mill in Santiago de Veraguas, told AFP.
Panama City's international airport, a major hub for the region, was temporarily closed.
Several flights were diverted to other airports as a precaution, according to the Civil Aeronautics Authority.
Big aftershocks
Earthquakes are rare in Panama and usually occur in the western province of Chiriqui, which borders Costa Rica.
Images shared by local media showed that part of a hotel had collapsed in the town of Penonome, 150km south-west of Panama City.
[[nid:1552124]]
A church in Penonome was also seriously damaged, and other buildings showed cracks, according to local reports.
A road in Veraguas province had cracks, according to images released by the local press.
More than a dozen large aftershocks, one above magnitude 6.0, were recorded by the local geosciences institute.
Writing on X, Panamanian President Jose Raul Mulino called for calm.
"What happened should not be used to generate alarms and disorder," he said, adding that he had called for a report on the damage.
The Education Ministry announced the suspension of classes in schools nationwide.
The Panamanian quake was at least the fourth earthquake this year in Latin America to exceed magnitude 7.0, following back-to-back devastating earthquakes in Venezuela's Guaira region in June and a powerful earthquake in western Colombia in August.

Title: Sarawak honours five helicopter crash victims posthumously
Article:
KUCHING: Five victims of the Air Medical Services (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, on Sept 8 have been posthumously awarded the Pegawai Bintang Sarawak (PBS) in recognition of their service and sacrifice.
They were Alexon Adit Henry, Debra Moset, Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, Jessie Paya Jok and Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham.
The awards were presented in conjunction with the 80th birthday celebration of Sarawak Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar today.
A total of 1,350 individuals received state honours, decorations and medals at the ceremony.
Leading the list was Sabah and Sarawak Chief Judge Datuk Azizah Nawawi, who received the Panglima Negara Bintang Sarawak (PNBS), which carries the title Datuk Seri.
Also receiving the PNBS were Yang di-Pertua Dewan Negara Datuk Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah, Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) pro-chancellor Datuk Abdul Wahab Aziz and ABM Fujiya Berhad chairman Datuk Tay Ah Ching.
Four individuals received the Panglima Gemilang Bintang Kenyalang (PGBK), which carries the title Datuk. They were Court of Appeal judge Dean Wayne Daly, Sarawak Deputy Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Sebastian Ting Chiew Yew, Sarawak State Legislative Assembly Deputy Speaker Datuk Idris Buang and senior private secretary to the Sarawak governor Datuk Seri Syed Hamzah Syed Paie.
Meanwhile, six individuals received the Darjah Jasa Bakti Sarawak (DJBS), which carries the title Datu. They included Sarawak Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Ministry permanent secretary Morshidi Fredrick, Agriculture Department director Dominic Chunggat, Sarawak Islamic Religious Department director Ustaz Mual Suaud and Sarawak Research and Development Council (SRDC) general manager Ts Dr Peter Morin Michael Paong.
Another 22 individuals received the Panglima Setia Bintang Sarawak (PSBS), which carries the title Datuk. They included senators Rita Sarimah Patrick Insol and Susan Chemerai Anding, and Krian assemblyman Friday Belik.
Also among the recipients were UiTM Sarawak rector Prof Dr Firdaus Abdullah, Universiti Malaysia Sarawak vice-chancellor Prof Dr Ahmad Hata Rasit, Sarawak Education Department director Omar Mahli and Sarawak Health Department director Dr Veronica Lugah.
Bukit Aman Management Department director Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah, First Infantry Division commander Major General Mohd Sobirin Mohd Yusof and SMD Semiconductor Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Shariman Jamil also received the PSBS.
The PSBS was also awarded posthumously to Sibat Buyong.

Title: RTD welcomes 2027 Budget road safety measures, including victim compensation
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs who cause accidents will be forced to compensate victims under proposed amendments to the Road Transport Act 1987.
Road Transport Department (RTD) director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the amendment was among three key 2027 Budget initiatives welcomed by the Transport Ministry and RTD to strengthen road safety and protect public welfare.
"This measure will not only strengthen action against offenders but also ensure that victims and affected families receive the appropriate redress," he said in a statement.
He said the ministry and RTD welcomed the mandatory implementation of telematics systems for commercial vehicles to monitor speed, location and risky driving patterns, including the potential integration of alcohol detection devices.
"The voluntary implementation phase until 2027 will give commercial vehicle operators time to prepare, while a driver database is being developed to support more effective enforcement," he said.
Aedy Fadly said RTD welcomed the announcement of special assistance of RM1,000 for taxi and school bus drivers, to be disbursed from next week using proceeds from bids for the H series special registration number.
"This initiative demonstrates that revenue collected by RTD is channelled back to benefit the people, particularly drivers who play an important role in the country's transport services," he said.
The ministry and RTD are working with relevant agencies, including the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), to conduct health screenings for commercial vehicle drivers to safeguard their safety and welfare.
When tabling the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said 28 deaths involving drunk or drug-impaired drivers had been recorded up to August this year.
Anwar said the government would make telematics systems compulsory for commercial vehicles and that Perkeso would provide health screening vouchers for commercial vehicle drivers. - BERNAMA
