Title: Two 22-year-old women die in car fire after collision with lorry in Yong Peng
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Oct 10 — Two 22-year-old women were burnt to death when their car caught fire following a collision with a lorry at Batu 1, Jalan Yong Peng-Ayer Hitam, yesterday afternoon.
The victims were identified as the driver of the Perodua Myvi, Siti Nur Batrisya Mohd Khalid, and her front seat passenger, Siti Nurmaisarah Abd Jalil.
Ayer Hitam Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Mohd Shamin Mohamed Salikin said they received an emergency call at 4.21pm, and a team arrived at the scene four minutes later.
He said when firefighters arrived, they found the car about 80 per cent burnt, with both victims trapped in the driver and front passenger seats.
“The team carried out firefighting operations before extricating both victims using special equipment. They were pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry medical officers,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Mohd Shamin said both victims were found burnt beyond recognition. Three men in their 30s in the Isuzu lorry were uninjured.
The operation, involving 16 personnel from the Ayer Hitam and Yong Peng Fire and Rescue Stations, ended at 6.38pm. The bodies were handed over to the police for further action. — Bernama

Title: SME association says Budget 2027 offers support, but warns of ‘cumulative’ cost pressures
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — The Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Association of Malaysia has welcomed the government’s Budget 2027 initiatives aimed at bolstering domestic consumption and promoting investment but cautioned that the cumulative cost of doing business remains the sector's most significant hurdle.
The association's president Chin Chee Seong said that while the Budget introduces various measures to support businesses, the government must ensure these initiatives deliver measurable improvements to SME cash flow, productivity and competitiveness.
“SMEs are not asking simply for more money. We are asking for policies that deliver real and measurable results,” Chin told
Malay Mail
following the Budget announcement yesterday.
“Judge the Budget by actual outcomes, not the amount of money allocated. We must look at how many SMEs genuinely benefit, how many jobs are sustained, and whether Malaysian businesses become more productive, resilient, and competitive.”
Regarding the minimum wage increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000, Chin welcomed the exemption for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales below RM50 million.
However, he warned that smaller businesses would still face indirect cost pressures through supply chains.
“The 17.6 per cent wage increase could affect business margins, hiring, consumer prices, and employment.
“Higher wages must not come at the expense of jobs, business survival, and competitiveness,” he said, calling for a phased, sector-sensitive implementation supported by productivity improvements.
On the corporate tax reduction, Chin noted that the one-percentage-point cut provides limited relief, with maximum annual savings of RM6,000 — equivalent to RM500 monthly — which he argued does little to offset rising operating expenses.
“SMEs need direct operating-cost relief and better cash flow, not just lower taxes,” he added.
Chin also addressed the funding allocated for artificial intelligence (AI) and automation, as well as technical and vocational education and training (TVET).
While appreciative of the RM30 million allocation for 4,000 SMEs for AI and automation, he suggested the average allocation of RM7,500 per enterprise might be insufficient for meaningful transformation.
“AI success must be measured by actual cost savings, efficiency improvements, and productivity gains, not adoption numbers alone,” he stated.
Similarly, regarding the RM8 billion TVET allocation, he urged the government to allow businesses to participate directly in curriculum design and practical training to ensure the output matches industry needs in sectors such as electrical and electronics, precision manufacturing and logistics.
The association also raised concerns regarding financing.
While welcoming the increase in total loans and financing guarantees from RM50 billion to RM57 billion, Chin pointed out that strict eligibility requirements and slow approvals remain persistent barriers.
“Financing availability means little if SMEs cannot access it when needed. We urge the government to strengthen SJPP and CGC guarantees, simplify applications, and accelerate approvals,” he said.
Ultimately, Chin stressed that the business community faces simultaneous pressures from rising costs in utilities, rental, logistics and compliance.
He proposed that the government conduct a “cumulative SME cost and regulatory impact assessment” before implementing future major policy changes.
Chin also called for stronger enforcement against non-compliant foreign e-commerce sellers, including checks on import declarations, tax payments, SIRIM compliance and product safety standards to safeguard local businesses.
“We welcome foreign competition, but Malaysian SMEs must compete on a level playing field,” he said.

Title: Zara Qairina’s mum disputes diary entries expressing ‘hate’ towards her, says handwriting not daughter’s
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 10 — The mother of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir yesterday disputed the authenticity of several diary entries expressing hatred towards her, telling the Coroner's Court she had never seen her daughter write such things.
Noraidah Lamat, 46, said she disagreed that the entries must have been Zara Qairina's, since anyone could have written them.
During questioning by Inquest Conducting Officer Nahra Dollah on diary pages tendered as exhibits, Noraidah rejected the suggestion that entries bearing the phrase “Aku benci ibu” (I hate mother) reflected her daughter's feelings towards her.
“I disagree because I have never seen Zara Qairina's writing like this,” she said before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan yesterday in the inquest into the teenager's death.
When Nahra suggested that, logically, only Zara Qairina herself would have reason to write such words, Noraidah disagreed, maintaining that she knew her daughter and did not rule out the possibility that the entries could have been written by someone else.
Meanwhile, when referred to the next sheet of paper, which bore her name and the words “tidak payah melahirkan aku” (you didn't have to give birth to me), Noraidah again disagreed that the entry reflected Zara Qairina's feelings towards her.
She conceded that the entry used coarse, abusive language but maintained that it was not her daughter's writing.
When asked whether Zara Qairina's friends might have written the entry, Noraidah said she had never been informed that any of her daughter's friends had problems with her or harboured any resentment towards her.
Noraidah also confirmed that Zara Qairina had a habit of keeping a diary, which mostly revolved around friendships and daily life.
However, she said she had never read entries containing negative feelings towards her, such as those tendered in the proceedings.
Zara Qairina died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital on July 17, 2025, a day after the Form One student was found unconscious near a drain at her school hostel at 4am.
The inquest proceedings resume on October 12. — Bernama

Title: Fourteen remanded as police probe death of 18-year-old found by Gurun roadside
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 10 — Fourteen people aged between 16 and 24 have been remanded to assist investigations into the death of an 18-year-old man whose body was found by the roadside in Gurun on Thursday.
Bernama
reported Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan as saying that 12 of the suspects were remanded for six days, while two minors were remanded for five days.
The remand orders were issued by Magistrate Noor Fazlina Musa at the Sungai Petani Magistrates’ Court yesterday.
Police are investigating the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
The victim, identified by
Sinar Harian
as Muhammad Haikal Mohd Shahrilnizam, was found at about 8am near Jalan Harvard in Gurun.
He was wearing black-and-yellow sports attire and had injuries to his head and face.
Bernama
reported that the victim initially had no identification documents on him before authorities established his identity.
Police have not disclosed further details on the suspected motive or the alleged involvement of those remanded.

Title: Budget 2027: Grab aims to raise gig workers’ earnings without increasing fares
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Grab aims to increase the earnings of e-hailing drivers and p-hailing delivery partners from 2027 without affecting passenger fares under a proposed minimum earnings framework.
In a statement yesterday, Grab said an agreement in principle had been reached on a proposed minimum baseline rate for e-hailing and p-hailing workers.
“The Gig Consultative Council will continue its deliberations to determine the final rates,” it said.
Grab’s statement follows Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement during the tabling of Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday that the government and Grab would jointly fund a RM160 million package to boost the earnings and welfare of gig workers.
Under the package, median monthly net income for e-hailing drivers is expected to increase by up to RM227, while p-hailing delivery partners’ income is expected to rise by up to RM100.
Grab said other initiatives include a vehicle maintenance subsidy, starting with lubricants, to reduce operating costs by up to 35 per cent, as well as an interim safety incentive to help eligible e-hailing drivers cut regulatory insurance costs by up to 25 per cent.
The company also said its most active drivers and delivery partners would receive 100 per cent coverage for mandatory Social Security Organisation (SOCSO) contributions, while other partners would receive contribution subsidies of up to 50 per cent.
Grab said it will also work with the government to introduce a monthly transit pass offering discounted e-hailing rides to and from train stations, starting in the Klang Valley.
“By offering commuters discounted e-hailing rides to and from train stations, the initiative aims to improve access to fixed route public transportation while generating additional demand for driver-partners,” it said.
Grab executive director Rashid Shukor said improving the livelihoods of its driver and delivery partners remained a priority for the company.
“We understand that every ringgit matters, whether it comes from additional earning opportunities or savings on the everyday costs of working.
“In collaboration with the government, we are taking the lead in the industry to advance measures that can make a meaningful difference to our partners, while building a stronger and more sustainable gig economy,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Egypt to hold bilateral talks today as El-Sisi makes first state visit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Malaysia and Egypt will hold bilateral talks today to review progress in cooperation between the two countries and exchange views on regional and international issues.
In a Facebook post last night, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the meeting with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi would also witness the exchange of several memoranda of understanding between Malaysia and Egypt.
“After tabling the Fifth Madani Budget today, I proceeded directly to the Bunga Raya Complex at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to welcome the arrival of President of the Arab Republic of Egypt Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, who is on a state visit at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
“Welcome to Malaysia, President El-Sisi!” he said.
The Foreign Ministry said in a statement yesterday that El-Sisi was accompanied by Cabinet ministers and senior Egyptian government officials on his first state visit to Malaysia since assuming the presidency in June 2014.
Malaysia and Egypt established diplomatic relations in 1959.
In 2025, Egypt was Malaysia’s seventh-largest trading partner among African countries.
Bilateral trade amounted to RM3.08 billion (US$0.72 billion), with Malaysian exports to Egypt valued at RM2.55 billion (US$0.60 billion) and imports from Egypt totalling RM530 million (US$120 million).
From January to August 2026, total trade between the two countries rose by 74.7 per cent to RM3.49 billion (US$870 million). — Bernama

Title: Having a baby? Budget 2027 proposes up to RM3,000 tax relief for postnatal care
Real inclusion: How Budget 2027 benefits ordinary Malaysians in giving them a share of the country’s wealth and success
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled Budget 2027 yesterday, the fifth by his administration, appearing to shift greater focus towards ensuring that ordinary Malaysians benefit from economic growth and reforms pursued over the past four years.
The national budget totalling RM510 billion, up from RM470 billion in Budget 2026, was tabled amid elevated global fuel prices and Malaysia’s ageing population, and could be the final one before the 16th General Election (GE16).
After years of focusing on economic stability, fiscal discipline and reforms, Budget 2027 appears to place greater emphasis on ensuring that the gains from these efforts are felt by ordinary Malaysians in their daily lives, with living costs still pinching households.
To this end, Anwar has sought to boost household incomes through higher wages and cash aid, more support for businesses and stronger safety nets through tax reliefs and incentives in Budget 2027.
Reforms remain high on his administration’s agenda, with Anwar promising further measures to tighten oversight of government procurement and the management of public funds in 2027.
Here’s a snapshot of what makes Budget 2027:
Cash assistance and cost of living
The government will increase the allocation for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to RM16 billion, from RM15 billion.
STR recipients: All recipients will receive SARA of up to RM150 a month, or RM1,800 a year, benefiting up to nine million people.
Other adults: Malaysians aged 18 and above who are not STR recipients will receive Sara Madani of RM100 twice in 2027 — before Aidilfitri and ahead of the 70th anniversary of Merdeka.
Cheaper groceries: Fresh produce will be offered at prices up to 30 per cent lower at Jualan Rahmah Madani and Agro Madani sales
Rural supplies: RM250 million will be allocated to expand the distribution of essential goods to rural and interior areas, including six new locations.
Tax relief and take-home pay
Individual income tax relief will increase from RM9,000 to RM12,000, while tax rates will be lowered by one percentage point for selected income brackets.
The tax rate for income between RM70,000 and RM100,000 will fall to 18 per cent.
The rate for income between RM100,000 and RM150,000 will fall to 24 per cent.
The tax rate for income above RM1 million will be set at 30 per cent.
The government expects the changes to increase disposable income by up to RM1,600 for about five million taxpayers.
Tax relief will also be expanded to cover postnatal care, care expenses for parents and grandparents, sports shoes, tuition for children, subscriptions to artificial intelligence services, vaccinations and adoption costs for pets from registered centres.
Members of the public watching the live telecast of 2027 Budget by Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar in Parliament around Putrajaya Oct 9, 2026. — Picture by Choo Choy May.
Workers, minimum wage and gig workers
The minimum wage will increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month from June 2027, affecting more than four million workers.
Small and medium enterprises with annual sales below RM50 million will be given time to adjust their business models.
The government also announced a starting minimum wage of RM2,500 a month for semi-skilled occupations and graduates.
Government-linked investment companies and government-linked companies will raise their living-wage benchmark from RM3,100 to RM3,400 a month, benefiting about 230,000 workers.
For e-hailing and p-hailing workers, the government and Grab will jointly fund a RM160 million package from 2027 to improve net income and welfare.
This package is expected to increase median-level e-hailing drivers’ net income by up to RM227 a month and p-hailing riders’ income by up to RM100 a month. It also includes matching contributions to Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) schemes, with the government’s contribution rising from 35 per cent to 50 per cent if platform companies also contribute.
E-hailing and p-hailing workers will also be eligible for Employees Provident Fund (EPF) matching contributions of up to RM600 a year or RM6,000 over their lifetime.
All Malaysian citizens will also be registered automatically as EPF members when they turn 18.
Students and families
The government will increase several forms of education assistance and expand support for students.
School aid: Bantuan Awal Persekolahan or early schooling assistance will increase from RM150 to RM200 per pupil. A family with four school-going children will receive RM800.
University travel: FlySiswa Madani air-ticket assistance will increase from RM400 to RM500 for more than 60,000 public university students.
Form Six: Students will receive a living allowance of RM2,500, matching the allowance for matriculation students and benefiting about 90,000 students.
PTPTN loans: Borrowers earning RM2,500 or less a month can defer repayments in 2027. Those earning between RM2,500 and RM3,000 will pay a minimum of RM50 a month. Borrowers without arrears who repay regularly will receive a 10 per cent discount.
Affordable meals: Dapur Siswa Madani will be extended to polytechnics and teacher education institutes, with RM20 million for cooking equipment, food contributions and RM5 meals.
Student housing: The first phase of Universiti Malaya’s student residence is scheduled for completion in 2031, benefiting 10,000 students. The Retirement Fund Inc (KWAP) will invest RM750 million in Vista Kampus housing at six universities, including UniSZA and UiTM.
The government will also allocate RM800 million for higher education infrastructure, including lecture rooms, student residences and replacement of ageing equipment.
Schools, hospitals and public services
Education and healthcare remain among the largest areas of federal spending.
The Education Ministry will receive nearly RM69 billion, up from RM66.2 billion this year, Health Ministry will receive RM47.7 billion, the Higher Education Ministry will get RM19.1 billion and the Home Affairs and Defence ministries will each receive RM22 billion.
For schools, the allocation to repair and maintain all types of schools will double from RM1 billion to RM2 billion — am allocation that includes repairs for national schools, Chinese national-type schools, Tamil national-type schools and registered
rakyat
religious schools,
tahfiz
institutions and
pondok
schools.
A further RM1.3 billion will be provided to upgrade 682 dilapidated schools, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak.
The government also expects 3,500 additional classrooms to be completed by the end of this year to accommodate more Year One pupils.
For public healthcare, RM1.2 billion will be allocated to maintain and repair hospitals and clinics, while more than RM770 million will go towards modern medical equipment, including 400 new ambulances and upgraded haemodialysis facilities.
Nine new healthcare facilities will be built, including a specialist complex and day-treatment centre at Hospital Sultanah Aminah in Johor, a specialist dental centre in Kuching, and integrated health complexes in Gerik, Perak, and Rembau, Negeri Sembilan.
More than 9,000 contract doctors will be made permanent medical officers at public healthcare facilities next year. Paramedics and nurses will receive RM200 post-basic incentives monthly while Air Health Service staff will receive RM100 monthly.
The government will also introduce the MediAsas affordable medical plan in January 2027.
EPF members aged below 55 can pay their premiums using their Akaun Sejahera.
Meanwhile, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) with fewer than 75 employees will receive a first-year premium subsidy of RM200 per worker, capped at 50 workers per company.
The scheme is expected to benefit up to 200,000 workers.
PeKa B40 will continue offering free health screenings, medical equipment assistance and cancer-treatment incentives for STR recipients and their spouses aged 40 and above, with RM80 million allocated.
MySalam will also continue, while the Medical Aid Fund will increase from RM40 million to RM60 million.
The government expects the changes to increase disposable income by up to RM1,600 for about five million taxpayers. — Picture by Choo Choy May.
Help for senior citizens and people with disabilities
Welfare assistance for senior citizens will receive RM1.3 billion, benefiting nearly 200,000 recipients.
The monthly allowance for caring for bedridden people with disabilities and the chronically ill will increase from RM500 to RM600, while the income threshold for the disabled workers’ allowance will increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000.
Anwar also reduced the service tax rate for elderly care services from eight to six per cent, with a full exemption on fees up to RM96,000 annually. Some 8,000 caregivers will also be trained through an allocation of RM40 million under HRD Corp.
Pupils with special educational needs will also receive a higher allowance of RM200, while the teaching incentive for special education teachers will increase from RM250 to RM300 a month.
Two new Permata Kurnia centres — a Malaysian early intervention and education programme for children with autism — will be built in Melaka and Pahang, alongside more than 130 new Tabika Tunas Istimewa classes in rural areas.
Public transport and connectivity
Public transport users will benefit from continued subsidised passes and investments to improve services.
My50: The pass will continue for 300,000 Prasarana bus and rail users in the Klang Valley.
MyKomuter50: A new pass will benefit 40,000 KTM Komuter users, with average savings of up to RM160 a month.
Free passes: About 360,000 school pupils, people with disabilities and children below six will receive free passes.
Train services: The government will acquire 42 new train sets for ETS and KTM Komuter services. Prasarana will invest more than RM3.4 billion in a comprehensive rail-service recovery programme.
Bus services: RM270 million will be allocated to improve bus services in major cities, including links to 15 East Coast stations ahead of the East Coast Rail Link’s operation.
The first phase of the ECRL, from Kota Bharu to the Gombak Integrated Transport Terminal, is expected to begin operating in December 2026, while a bus station will also be built at the Kota Bharu ECRL station.
Roads, water, electricity and internet
Rural communities will receive RM3.3 billion for basic infrastructure, including roads, community facilities, clean water and electricity. The allocation for rural roads will rise to RM2.3 billion.
The National Non-Revenue Water programme will receive RM2.5 billion to replace 1,900km of ageing critical pipes.
Under the Jendela connectivity initiative, the government plans to extend 4G coverage to all Orang Asli villages, improve internet connectivity along 7,000km of roads and 1,700km of railway lines, and implement the Madani Undersea Cable project.
Road projects in Sabah and Sarawak will receive RM3.3 billion, while another RM350 million will be set aside for federal road maintenance by small contractors in both states.
Sabah will receive RM18.7 billion in federal allocation, up from RM17.6 billion this year, while Sarawak will receive RM16.2 billion, up from RM15.1 billion.
In Sabah, RM204 million will be spent on installing STATCOM systems at the Dam Road and Segaliud substations, while the Southern Link transmission line project will continue.
The federal government will also provide RM600 million to ensure electricity supply continuity in Sabah.
Flood protection and disaster aid
Flood mitigation projects will continue in Kuching, Sarawak, while the second phase of Sungai Golok in Kelantan and Sungai Kemaman in Terengganu.
Nearly RM320 million will be allocated to repair and upgrade slopes, drains and monsoon drains under local authorities, while the National Disaster Management Agency will receive RM260 million.
Financial assistance to repair homes damaged by disasters will increase from RM5,000 to RM10,000.
Housing and public amenities
Nearly RM1 billion will be allocated for Rumah Mesra Rakyat and Residensi Rakyat housing projects. Four new housing projects will be implemented in Kulai, Johor; Nilai, Negeri Sembilan; Paya Rumput, Melaka; and Lembah Pertang, Terengganu.
The Syarikat Jaminan Kredit Perumahan will provide housing financing guarantees of up to RM20 billion, aimed at helping 80,000 borrowers.
In Kuala Lumpur, the Dewan Bandaraya Kuala Lumpur (DBKL) will set aside RM400 million to create 120 acres of new green spaces, restore existing parks and upgrade public facilities and housing.
A 100-acre leased site in Bukit Kiara will be gazetted as a Federal Park.
DBKL will also build 22km of covered pedestrian walkways linking places including the National Mosque, Dataran Merdeka and Pasar Seni, as well as residential areas with shops, schools, clinics and public transport.
Civil servants and frontline services
The government has allocated RM2.3 billion for public servants’ quarters.
New army family housing will be built in Skudai, Johor, alongside quarters in Langkap, Perak, and Papar, Sabah, benefiting about 900 personnel.
Allowances for volunteers in Rela, volunteer fire brigades, volunteer police and civil defence will rise to RM9 an hour for volunteers and RM10.80 an hour for supervisors.
The RM339 million allocation is expected to benefit about 50,000 volunteers.

Title: Set on fire, thrown from cars: Iran’s women stunt performers break barriers
Article:
TEHRAN, Oct 9 — As evening falls at a Tehran skatepark, a woman calmly steps forward with her body ablaze, performing a daring stunt that challenges convention in front of an impressed Iranian audience.
Behind her, young women practise backward flips into a pit filled with foam, following the instructions of Nasrin Teymouri.
In her thirties, she leads Iran’s sole all-female stunt crew, a vital area of filmmaking traditionally controlled by men, but where Iranian women are increasingly establishing themselves.
“Until just a few years ago, men used to dress up as women to perform stunts in place of actresses,” said Teymouri with a smile, as she received AFP at a training session for the “Stunt Powerful” team in southern Tehran.
On graffiti-decorated ramps, a young girl wearing roller skates practises a few moves, while a young man gets ready to perform a stunt on his BMX bicycle.
The setting is unusual for this relatively traditional neighbourhood of the Iranian capital. A huge Islamic republic flag flutters in the distance, while the golden dome of a nearby mosque can be seen from the skatepark.
The site, dedicated to extreme sports and named “Navid Park” after its founder, opened a year ago.
Iranian coach and stunt woman Nasrin Teymouri (center R) teaches fire techniques to stunt performers Mojgan Nematollahi (C) and Arshia Teymouri (L) during a training session in in Tehran's skatepark, in the capital on September 25, 2026. — AFP pic
“Even prominent directors would bluntly tell us we couldn’t be stunt performers simply because we were women,” recalled Teymouri, who now appears in successful Iranian productions and trains male stunt performers, reflecting changing views in Iran.
“Eventually, they placed their trust in us” on film sets, she said.
“Because they saw our work, accepted it and liked it,” added Teymouri, who earns a living teaching gymnastics.
“In the past, our presence on set used to unsettle them”.
‘Afraid of everything’
Teymouri has inspired others, including Mahisa Babayi-Parsa, a nine-year-old who insisted she was not “afraid at all” when carrying out stunts.
“I’ve been set on fire twice. I’ve jumped from heights, tumbled down stairs, and even been ejected from a car,” she beamed.
The stunt crew, a tight-knit team of women and men, gathers for practice several times each month.
During rehearsals in which a woman is engulfed in flames, colleagues remain on standby with a fire extinguisher and a wet blanket, ready to intervene.
Iranian coach and stunt woman Nasrin Teymouri (R) teaches fire techniques to stunt performers Mojgan Nematollahi (C) and Arshia Teymouri (L) during a training session in in Tehran's skatepark, in the capital on September 25, 2026. — AFP pic
When a man prepares to be set alight for a bicycle stunt, women supervise the process, challenging established norms.
Mixed-gender participation remains banned in many sports in Iran, where men and women are not even permitted to visit the same gym.
“I’m someone who gets scared very easily: I’m afraid of heights and speed. I’m afraid of everything,” Teymouri said.
“But facing my fear gives me immense pleasure every time” and “that’s what drove me to survive in this profession,” she added, sporting sunglasses and a cap worn backwards. — AFP

Title: Civil servants to get RM1,500 aid, pensioners RM750 under Budget 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — A total of 1.3 million civil servants in Grade Utama B and below, including those on contract appointments, will receive RM1,500 in special financial assistance under Budget 2027.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the finance minister, announced the assistance when tabling the Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today.
More than one million government pensioners, including pensionable and non-pensionable veterans, will also receive RM750 each.
The payments will be made in two instalments, with disbursements scheduled before Aidilfitri and ahead of the 70th anniversary of Merdeka.
Separately, the government will provide RM750 each to 70,000 religious personnel in recognition of their service.
The recipients include KAFA and takmir teachers, imams, bilals, tok siak, noja and marbut.

Title: Rehda backs Budget 2027 housing measures but calls for more action on rising costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda)
has
welcomed measures in Budget 2027 to support homeownership, while urging the government to do more to address rising development costs and housing affordability.
Its president, Datuk Zaini Yusoff, said in a statement that the expanded stamp duty exemptions for first-time homebuyers would help reduce the upfront cost of buying a home.
Under the measures announced, buyers of properties priced up to RM500,000 would receive full stamp duty exemptions on instruments of transfer and loan agreements.
For properties priced up to RM750,000, the exemption would cover the first RM500,000, with a 50 per cent exemption on the remaining amount.
“These measures will help ease the upfront financial burden of aspiring homeowners,” he said.
Zaini said Rehda hoped the government would continue reviewing the eligibility thresholds in line with prevailing house prices and market conditions, including considering extending the incentives to properties priced up to RM1 million.
The association also welcomed stamp duty exemptions for rehabilitating abandoned housing projects, saying
they
could help revive projects and provide relief to affected purchasers.
It further welcomed RM20 billion in housing financing guarantees under Syarikat Jaminan Kredit Perumahan, which is expected to benefit about 80,000 first-time homebuyers, particularly those with irregular incomes.
“Improving access to end-financing remains crucial in addressing the challenges
faced by prospective purchasers,”
Zaini said.
Rehda said the government’s continued commitment to affordable housing was also encouraging, with nearly RM1 billion allocated for Rumah Mesra Rakyat and Programme Residensi Rakyat.
It cited affordable housing initiatives by Petronas and the Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil development as further efforts to expand opportunities for Malaysians, particularly lower-income groups.
The association also welcomed the extension until December 31, 2030, of investment tax allowances of up to 100 per cent for qualifying green technology projects and assets.
It said the incentives could encourage more sustainable practices, especially among smaller developers facing higher implementation costs.
However, Rehda remained concerned about rising development
costs, including construction materials, labour and regulatory compliance,
and called for further measures to ease
the
pressure.
“More needs to be done to ensure a more holistic change in housing affordability, such as
the review of
all related charges imposed by the federal and state governments, including infrastructure, utility, statutory, regulatory and compliance charges.
“These costs remain a challenge in developers’ efforts
in addressing
affordability, and we reaffirm our commitment to engage with the government and all relevant parties to meet this goal,” Zaidi said.
Rehda also urged the government to reconsider reviving the Home Ownership Campaign, particularly to help sell completed but unsold residential properties while giving more Malaysians the opportunity to own a home.
The Home Ownership Campaign (HOC) is a government-supported initiative designed to help more Malaysians buy homes. It has offered incentives such as stamp duty exemptions and developer discounts, while encouraging sales of eligible residential properties.

Title: PLUS to close Bangi Toll Plaza road shoulder for widening works until June 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — PLUS Malaysia Berhad (PLUS) will temporarily close the road shoulder after the exit lane of the Bangi Toll Plaza towards Bandar Baru Bangi from today until June 28 next year to facilitate road widening works.
In a statement today, PLUS said the works were scheduled to take approximately eight months as part of the company’s ongoing efforts to improve highway facilities and enhance users’ comfort.
The closure will only be implemented during off-peak hours, from 10 pm to 5.30 am, to minimise disruption to traffic flow in the area.
Motorists passing through the area are advised to slow down, comply with safety signs and the stipulated speed limits, and follow instructions from personnel at the site.
Users are also advised to plan their journeys and obtain the latest traffic updates through the PLUS app, the company’s official social media platforms, including its X account @plustrafik, and electronic message signs (VMS) at selected locations.
For current traffic information or emergency assistance on the highway, users can contact PLUSLine at 1800-88-0000. — Bernama

Title: E-Commerce Bill to protect small traders, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government will table an E-Commerce Bill at the next parliamentary sitting to strengthen accountability among online platforms and sellers, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the government was urgently examining legislative and enforcement measures to protect micro, small and medium enterprises from unfair competition and ensure goods purchased by consumers were safe.
“The government takes seriously the concerns of small traders over the presence of foreign e-commerce companies entering the domestic market without adequate oversight and enforcement,” he said when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
The fifth Madani Budget, themed “Malaysia Madani: Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi”, is the second budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Home, Defence Ministries each allocated RM22b
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Home Ministry and Defence Ministry have each been allocated RM22 billion under Budget 2027, tabled in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said RM7.1 billion of the total allocation would be channelled to procure and maintain assets for the armed forces, police, and uniformed agencies under the Home Ministry.
He said the government had also agreed to build several new facilities, including the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) Johor headquarters in Tanjung Kupang, the General Operations Force (GOF) 19th Battalion Complex in Cheras, the Keningau Immigration Office in Sabah, and three new police stations in Sungai Rambai, Melaka; Tanjung Malim, Perak; and Batu Lintang, Sri Aman, Sarawak.
“An allocation of RM490 million will be provided to the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), while security screening at airports will be tightened, including mandatory drug and alcohol tests for pilots and flight crew.
“A total of 48 new body and baggage scanners will be installed at Kuala Lumpur International Airport, Penang International Airport and Kota Kinabalu International Airport,” he said when tabling the budget themed “Reaching for the Sky, Rooted in the Ground”.
Anwar also said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had blocked more than 5.7 billion scam-related calls and SMS messages.
He said the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) would develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered application to enable the public to check suspicious phone numbers, bank accounts and links before making transactions, allowing scams and cybercrimes to be detected earlier.
“The Royal Malaysia Police’s D11 Division is also strengthening the Malaysia Internet Crime Against Children system, which is equipped with advanced analytical capabilities to detect perpetrators and child sexual exploitation networks at an earlier stage.
“The Safe Internet Campaign will also be intensified in all schools, with a focus on addressing cyberbullying and child exploitation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027 draws positive response from ministers over focus on living costs, wages and public services
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Budget 2027 has drawn broadly positive reactions from Cabinet ministers, who welcomed its emphasis on easing the cost of living, raising wages and improving public services, as the government seeks to ensure that the benefits of economic growth reach ordinary Malaysians.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the measures reflected public feedback gathered through nationwide engagement sessions, particularly concerns over rising living costs and the need for better wages.
“Our effort in Budget 2027 is to ensure that the spillover gains from the country successfully becoming a strong trading nation are passed down to the people,” he said at a press conference following the budget's tabling in Parliament today.
“The government has listened to feedback received from various parties, through the budget roadshows, engagement sessions, and the grievances brought to us,” he added.
“Today we can see how we outlined our focus areas during the pre-budget sessions to address cost-of-living issues and improve wage quality across the country.”
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, earlier tabled Budget 2027, which places greater emphasis on boosting household disposable income and supporting middle-income earners alongside continued economic reforms.
Among the measures announced were an increase in the minimum wage to RM2,000 per month, higher entry-level pay floors for graduates and semi-skilled workers, tax relief for middle-income earners and expanded direct cash assistance programmes.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi welcomed the budget’s focus on technical and vocational education and training (TVET), saying the measures would help address financial pressures faced by the M40 while improving employment prospects for skilled workers.
“Overall, this budget reflects the government’s strong commitment to addressing the problems faced by the M40 group, whose disposable income and purchasing power have been under pressure because of high financial commitments,” he said in his initial reaction.
Zahid said the RM8 billion allocation for TVET would allow the government to expand training in specialised fields, including robotics, and improve workers’ employability.
“We will expand courses that are appropriate to market demand, so that the skills acquired can lead to better employment prospects,” he said, also welcoming provisions for higher wages for skilled workers.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi speaks during a press conference at Parliament in Kuala Lumpur on October 9, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said his ministry had received a slight increase in its allocation to RM12.68 billion, stressing that the priority was to ensure programmes delivered meaningful benefits to target groups.
Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil, meanwhile, welcomed measures to assist the M40 and B40 groups, as well as support for the local film industry and continued investment in digital infrastructure.
“For the first time, the film sector has received interesting support,” he said, expressing hope that Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya would see more filmmaking activity, which could contribute to economic growth and job creation.
Fahmi also highlighted the government's recognition of National Information Dissemination Centres (NADI) and the importance of continued investment in the Jalinan Digital Negara (JENDELA) initiative and submarine cable connectivity.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad described the RM47.7 billion allocation for his ministry as a reasonable basis for continuing healthcare reforms, including addressing longstanding staffing shortages and improving medical facilities.
He welcomed the provision of more than 9,000 permanent positions for contract doctors, as well as increased post-basic incentive payments for 47,000 paramedics and nurses.
Dzulkefly also highlighted RM1.2 billion for maintaining and repairing public hospitals and clinics, saying the additional resources would help the ministry improve healthcare services.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad speaks during a press conference following the tabling of Budget 2027 at Parliament in Kuala Lumpur on October 9, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi welcomed increased funding for infrastructure and smaller contractors, despite his ministry receiving a relatively modest 1.78 per cent increase in its overall allocation.
“What is important is how we use it. We have many programmes and projects,” he said, pointing to additional opportunities for G1 to G4 contractors and RM800 million for construction, roads and infrastructure, including RM350 million for Sabah and Sarawak contractors.
Nanta said allocations for district engineers had increased from RM30 million to RM40 million, allowing smaller infrastructure problems to be addressed more quickly without further approvals.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi (centre) speaks to members of the media during a press conference following the groundbreaking ceremony for the third tunnel and widening project of the Kuala Lumpur-Karak (KLK) Highway at KM36.9 eastbound on August 20, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
He also welcomed provisions for motorcycle shelters, closed-circuit television cameras along PLUS highways and 50 electric vehicle charging points, saying the measures would improve facilities for road users despite government spending constraints.
Beyond the sector-specific allocations, Budget 2027 also increased funding for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to RM16 billion, from RM15 billion, while raising individual income tax relief from RM9,000 to RM12,000.
The measures reflect what appears to be a central theme of Anwar’s fifth budget — ensuring that the gains from economic growth and reforms pursued over the past four years translate into higher household incomes, reduced financial pressures and tangible improvements in the daily lives of Malaysians.

Title: Malaysia’s approved investments rise 11.7pc to RM218.5b in first half of 2026, says PM
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Malaysia’s approved investments rose 11.7 per cent to RM218.5 billion in the first half of 2026, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar, also the finance minister, said Malaysia was on track to reach a new record high for the third consecutive year.
“Government-linked investment companies (GLICs) have been entrusted with building domestic economic resilience and enhancing the capabilities of local companies in high-value sectors.
“For example, Sime Darby Property, the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) and the Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) have established the RM1.25 billion New Economy Venture Fund to develop data centres and logistics assets in Elmina, Selangor,” he said when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Meanwhile, he said Khazanah Nasional Bhd and the Retirement Fund (KWAP) had invested RM1.2 billion to help local semiconductor companies move up the value chain. “This includes a collaboration between Khazanah and the Selangor state government on an investment fund for semiconductor development in Selangor,” he added.
The fifth Madani Budget, themed “Malaysia Madani: Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi” (Reaching for the Sky, Rooted in the Ground), is the second budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP). — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: RM2.62b aid for paddy farmers, incentives for fishermen, smallholders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government is allocating RM2.62 billion in aid to paddy farmers under Budget 2027, covering various subsidies and incentives to increase rice production and safeguard their welfare.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the assistance would enable paddy farmers to receive benefits of about RM4,300 per hectare of paddy field, including subsidies for seeds, fertiliser, pesticides, ploughing costs and paddy prices.
He said the government had agreed to increase the paddy harvesting incentive from RM50 to RM100 per hectare per season, while the ploughing incentive, which had been increased to RM300, would be maintained and extended to paddy farmers in Sabah and Sarawak.
“To rehabilitate and rejuvenate paddy fields, RM20 million will be provided to supply foliar fertiliser for more than 10,000 hectares of paddy fields.
“The Five-Season Padi Cultivation in Two Years Project is crucial to ensuring the continuity of the country’s rice supply, and work to upgrade irrigation systems in 15 paddy field blocks is progressing according to schedule. In addition, the Pedu Dam rehabilitation project in Kedah is expected to be completed by the end of 2027,” he said when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
For the fisheries and fishing sector, he said the government would increase the number of special boat licence holders from 17,000 to 20,000 fishermen, with an allocation of RM30 million, while providing aquaculture project grants and RM40 million in financing through Agrobank.
Eligible fishermen will also continue to enjoy subsidised diesel at RM1.65 per litre, while RM178 million will be allocated, among others, for catch incentives and a monthly Cost of Living Allowance of up to RM300.
Anwar said the government had allocated RM300 million to strengthen cooperation with state governments in implementing agrofood projects, in addition to providing more than RM1 billion in financing to agro-entrepreneurs through Agrobank, Bank Rakyat and the Malaysia Cooperative Societies Commission.
For smallholders in the oil palm sector, the government is providing RM100 million in hybrid financing for replanting involving 4,500 smallholders, as well as RM200 million in soft financing, with smallholders bearing only a two per cent interest rate and being granted a four-year repayment deferment.
The allocation for rehabilitating farm roads will also be doubled from RM50 million to RM100 million, while RM30 million will be provided to curb diseases and pest attacks affecting crops, including oil palm, cocoa and pepper.
The government has also agreed to increase the Rubber Production Incentive from RM3 to RM3.30 per kilogramme, which is expected to benefit more than 300,000 rubber smallholders.
Anwar said the government had also approved RM1.26 billion for 2027 to strengthen Felda’s finances, maintain roads and provide housing for the Felda community.
He said the average net income of Felda settlers had increased from RM2,272 per month in 2023 to RM3,800 this year, while 109,000 settlers now held land titles. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: RM8b for TVET, 30,000 new job opportunities via BAKAT Madani
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government has allocated RM8 billion for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) across ministries under Budget 2027 to enhance the skills and employability of young people.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was also targeting 30,000 new job opportunities through the BAKAT Madani initiative next year, including through the participation of private companies.
He said the initiative was launched following the commitment of six government-linked investment companies (GLICs), Petronas and the network of government-linked companies (GLCs) to provide training and quality job opportunities for 25,000 youths.
“To encourage greater participation by private companies, tax deductions will be granted to companies implementing BAKAT Madani training programmes from June 29, 2026 to December 31, 2030,” he said when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said that under the overall skills development initiative, HRD Corp, with an allocation of RM3 billion, would offer three million skills training opportunities, including for continuing professional development among professionals.
He said the Skills Development Fund Corporation (PTPK) had allocated RM500 million to finance trainees enrolled in skills training programmes at public and private skills training institutes registered with the corporation.
In addition, Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) would train and place 1,000 Bumiputera youths in high-growth sectors, while trainees skilled in electrical wiring at GIATMARA would help repair the wiring in 20,000 homes belonging to poor families.
The Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) would train 10,000 youths in robotics and digital technology to create career opportunities and reduce dependence on foreign labour.
Anwar said ADTEC JTM would provide graduates with a pathway to high-skilled automotive careers through the Advanced Automotive Technology programme, while community colleges would continue to offer short courses to tahfiz students as a pathway to employment, entrepreneurship and higher education.
Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) personnel of other ranks who have completed their service will also be provided with skills training through collaborations with institutions such as the Universiti Kuala Lumpur Malaysian Institute of Aviation Technology (UniKL MIAT) and Akademi Laut Malaysia (ALAM).
Meanwhile, he said the government had increased the allocation for the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (MITRA) to RM150 million, prioritising training and employment opportunities for Indian youths in fields such as industrial automation, technology and aircraft maintenance. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar: Registration to open next week for affordable smart city Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has announced that the affordable housing township Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil will be developed as a residential area complete with amenities, including a vertical school.
During the tabling of Budget 2027 today, he said registration for the first phase of the proposed 17,000-unit housing development will open on Monday.
Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said nearly RM1 billion has also been allocated for projects under the People-Friendly Homes (Rumah Mesra Rakyat) and People's Residency Programme (Program Residensi Rakyat).
“Four new housing projects will be implemented in Kulai, Johor; Nilai, Negeri Sembilan; Paya Rumput, Melaka; and Lembah Pertang, Terengganu,” he said.
Anwar also announced that the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) will provide housing financing guarantees of up to RM20 billion.
“This guarantee will assist 80,000 first-time homebuyers, particularly the self-employed who do not have a fixed income,” he said.
The SJKP is a federal government-backed programme under the Finance Ministry designed to help first-time homebuyers — especially those with irregular, non-fixed or informal incomes — secure housing loans from participating banks.

Title: Ringgit gains against US dollar as Budget 2027 underscores fiscal discipline
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The ringgit closed higher against the US dollar today, supported by the government’s commitment to fiscal consolidation under Budget 2027, an analyst said.
At 6pm, the ringgit climbed to 4.0830/0875 against the greenback from yesterday’s close of 4.0890/0940.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Malaysia’s fiscal deficit is expected to narrow to 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) next year from an estimated 3.6 per cent in 2026. “The expected narrowing of the fiscal deficit suggests that the government remains committed to fiscal discipline, which can effectively help bolster confidence among traders and investors towards the ringgit,” he told Bernama today.
At the close, the ringgit traded mixed against a basket of major and ASEAN currencies.
The local note rose against the Japanese yen to 2.5791/5821 from 2.5834/5867 at yesterday’s close, but dipped against the British pound to 5.4063/4123 from 5.3930/3996 and eased against the euro to 4.5807/5858 from 4.5719/5775 previously.
Against its Asean peers, the local note climbed against the Indonesian rupiah to 228.1/228.4 from 228.2/228.6, but remained unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.50/6.51.
It edged down against the Singapore dollar to 3.1896/1934 from 3.1893/1934 at Thursday’s close, and slid against the Thai baht to 12.1735/1909 from 12.1371/1563 previously. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Health minister vows to complete 9,000 contract-to-permanent doctor transitions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Health Ministry (MoH) will complete the process of appointing 9,000 contract doctors to permanent positions throughout 2027, effectively ending the interim contract doctor system, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said.
He said the initiative would require a somewhat different management approach to expedite the appointments while taking into account the stipulated requirements and the respective recruitment groups or cohorts of doctors.
“We will implement this in a way that may be somewhat innovative to ensure it is addressed as soon as possible. This requires some changes in management, explanation and approach. Don’t worry, we will put an end to it in 2027,” he told reporters after the tabling of Budget 2027 in Parliament today.
When tabling the budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that more than 9,000 contract doctors would be offered permanent positions next year, while doctors who complete their housemanship in the future would be offered permanent posts as medical officers.
Anwar also said that since 2023, the Madani Government had appointed more than 15,000 contract doctors to permanent positions, including 4,000 this year.
Asked whether the initiative could resolve the shortage of doctors, Dzulkefly described it as a positive step that could help address the healthcare workforce challenges faced by the ministry, particularly this year.
He said the RM47.7 billion allocated to the ministry under Budget 2027 comprised RM40.95 billion for operating expenditure and RM6.75 billion for development, enabling it to continue its healthcare reform agenda.
Among the initiatives to strengthen the healthcare workforce was an increase in the Post-Basic Incentive Payment from RM100 to RM200 a month, benefiting 47,000 paramedics and nurses, as well as an increase in the Air Health Services Incentive Payment from RM30 to RM100.
On healthcare services in remote areas, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak, Dzulkefly said MoH would continue to strengthen service delivery in line with the goal of Universal Health Coverage (UHC), ensuring that no one was left behind.
On a proposal for the ministry to own helicopters for air medical services, he said it preferred leasing them as this was more cost-effective and would spare the ministry the burden of maintaining the assets.
Asked whether the country’s healthcare facilities were under pressure due to the haze, Dzulkefly said ministry facilities remained capable of handling the increase in cases related to air pollution, although respiratory cases had risen significantly.
He advised the public to avoid outdoor activities, particularly when Air Pollutant Index (API) readings exceeded 160 or 200, and to minimise exposure to polluted air, especially among children, the elderly and those with pre-existing medical conditions. — Bernama

Title: ‘Today is for the rakyat, tomorrow is for the wife’: Syed Saddiq’s Budget 2027 reply amuses social media
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Muar Member of Parliament Syed Saddiq Abdul Rahman left local social media users amused following his response to a post on Threads.
The 34-year-old, who was present at today’s tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at Parliament, caught the attention of a Threads user who praised him for finding the time to attend despite his wedding ceremony taking place tomorrow.
“Today is for the rakyat, tomorrow is for the wife. (I) need to show up for both,” Syed Saddiq wrote in response to the post.
His response garnered over 170,000 views with over 12,000 likes along with comments from social media users amused by his choice of words.
https://www.threads.com/@syedsaddiq/post/DeRMNJelDwS
“He mentions ‘wife’ referring to someone else but I’m the one who’s feeling the butterflies,” commented user bloombae.byainawanie.
“From fiancée, to future wife to now just wife, so cute,” commented user nadhrahy_.
“Wow, after this we will be hearing the word ‘wife’ more often,” user sue_saraana96 commented.
Apart from local social media users, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul was also heard wishing “
Selamat Pengantin Baru Muar
” (“Congratulations on your wedding, Muar”) at the end of the Budget 2027 tabling, referring to Syed Saddiq’s constituency.
Tomorrow will mark the main wedding ceremony between Syed Saddiq and singer-actress Bella Astillah, which will take place at the 118th floor of the Merdeka 118.
A special dinner reception will follow on October 18 at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (Mitec).
The couple also announced two public wedding receptions, dubbed Kenduri Rakyat (people’s feast), in Muar, Johor, on October 25 and Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, on October 31.
The couple invited members of the public to share in their happiness.

Title: Sabah, with RM18.6b in allocations, hails 2027 budget as alleviating burden for all Malaysians
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 9 — Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor described the National 2027 Budget as a comprehensive budget that alleviates the people's financial burden and reflects the strength of the country's economy.
He said the budget that was proposed earlier today saw benefitted Malaysians through tax reductions and incentives for civil servants, businesses and all segments of society.
“It demonstrates the strength of our country's economy and financial position, despite the impact of the ongoing crisis in West Asia,” he said after watching the live broadcast of the tabling of the National 2027 Budget at Menara Kinabalu today.
In Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s proposed budget, Sabah continues to be the biggest recipient of federal allocations with RM18.6 billion for next year, an increase of 6.25 per cent compared to RM17.6 billion for this year.
In addition, Anwar said road projects in Sabah and Sarawak would continue with an allocation of RM3.3 billion under the 2027 Budget.
He also announced that the government had agreed to double the number of Public Service Department (JPA) scholarships offered to students from Sabah and Sarawak.
“This means that 4,200 students from Sabah and Sarawak will have the opportunity to pursue higher education at universities each year,” he said.
On boosting power supply system, he said the government has also agreed to install Static Synchronous Compensator (STATCOM) systems at the Dam Road and Segaliud Main Intake Substations at a cost of RM204 million.
The Southern Link Transmission Line project will also proceed as a long-term measure to ensure the sustainability of electricity supply in Sabah.
Road infrastructure along the borders of Sabah, Sarawak and Kalimantan will also continue to be upgraded to facilitate two-way movement.
Anwar also reiterated that the resolution of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) with the two east Malaysian state was to be viewed as part of the national covenant and promised that the interim payment of RM1.5 billion will be settled before the end of the year, while negotiations with Sabah and Sarawak will continue to finalise a fair and sustainable annual formula.
Also watching the live telecast with Hajiji were Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun, State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman, assistant ministers and senior state government officers.

Title: Lim Guan Eng calls Budget 2027 Anwar’s ‘most reform-minded’ yet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today described Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s fifth Madani Budget as the “most reform-minded” budget yet.
Lim, who is also Bagan MP, said expanding the social safety net to gig workers, persons with disabilities and senior citizens, providing more inclusive funding allocations and adjusting personal income tax rates to address past injustices were steps in the right direction.
“These initial steps of budgetary reforms give hope that there will be more future substantial meaningful reforms in the pipeline that will contain cost of living increases, creating sustainable economic growth especially for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and generating prosperity for all by ensuring that there is more money to spend for Malaysian households,” he said in a statement on Facebook.
Still, Lim said more needed to be done, particularly by allocating 10 per cent of total Bumiputera allocations to non-Bumiputera communities without reducing existing Bumiputera funding.
He said this would ensure a fairer and more equitable distribution of taxpayers’ money to non-Bumiputera communities, which he claimed previous governments had neglected.
Earlier, Anwar tabled the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat, outlining the government’s spending plans and direction for the coming year.
Themed “Malaysia Madani:
Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi
(Reaching for the Sky, Rooted in the Ground),” Budget 2027 is the second Budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan (RMK13), which serves as the national development framework for the 2026-2030 period.

Title: Budget 2027: Medical groups hail end to contract doctor system, enhanced public-private synergy but seek more on retention
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Healthcare stakeholders had mixed responses to the national health allocations announced in Budget 2027, with the Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) applauding the move to end the contract doctor system while highlighting critical gaps in workforce retention
The Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM), meanwhile, welcomed measures to boost public-private cooperation.
The Ministry of Health’s allocation has increased to RM47.7 billion, from RM46.5 billion in 2026.
MMA president Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan described the commitment to end the contract doctor system as a major win for the profession, noting that over 9,000 contract doctors are set to be offered permanent positions in 2027.
“This is a significant milestone and addresses one of MMA’s longstanding calls. We commend the Government for taking this important step towards providing greater job security and career certainty for our young doctors,” he said.
He, however, noted that permanent appointments must be accompanied by a broader strategy to retain healthcare workers.
Malaysia faces a shortage of nearly 11,000 specialists, he said, with demand for specialist care expected to rise amid the growing burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and an ageing population.
“We cannot afford to lose more specialists when we urgently need to train and retain more of them,” he said, calling for greater investment in specialist and subspecialist training, career progression, fair remuneration and better working conditions.
MMA also said more emphasis should be placed on strengthening primary healthcare to tackle NCDs.
The country’s network of private general practitioners remains underutilised and could play a greater role in prevention, early detection and long-term disease management, Sivanaesan said.
“Strengthening primary care is essential to reducing avoidable hospital admissions and easing pressure on specialist services,” he said.
Sivanaesan said the success of Budget 2027 should be measured not only by its allocations, but by improvements in patient care, waiting times, workforce retention and access to healthcare.
MMA reiterated its call for a national healthcare workforce distribution dashboard, providing transparent information on staffing levels and shortages at individual public hospitals and clinics. The data could support workforce planning and help direct resources to areas of greatest need, it said.
The association also noted that the RM1.2 billion allocation for hospital and clinic maintenance was unchanged from 2026, despite ageing facilities and growing maintenance needs.
It called for sufficient funding to address manpower shortages in Sabah and Sarawak, including better incentives and career opportunities, and reiterated its call to restore the previous percentage-based Regional Incentive Payment.
Meanwhile, APHM president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh welcomed measures to reduce patient waiting times, including a RM200 million allocation for outsourcing patients to other hospitals and expanded sessional arrangements for private-sector specialists, with the maximum engagement period extended.
APHM also welcomed Budget 2027’s reflection of work on billing transparency, saying it looked forward to further discussions with stakeholders on implementation.
Dr Kuljit said the e-CKAPS portal, which is due to enable private healthcare facilities to be licensed entirely online from 2027, targets a reduction of up to 65 per cent in processing times.
He said faster licensing could also support Malaysia’s medical tourism sector.
“What matters most is not the size of the budget increase but the outcome for patients.
“APHM stands ready to work closely with the Health Ministry and other stakeholders to turn these measures into real improvements on the ground,” he said.

Title: Four injured after lorry crashes into 11 vehicles in Shah Alam
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 9 — Four people were injured in an accident involving a lorry and 11 other vehicles at Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, Alam Budiman here today.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department was informed of the crash at about 4.30pm and immediately dispatched personnel to the scene.
“The accident left a man and a woman with serious head injuries, while two other male victims sustained minor injuries,” he said in a statement.
Ashrul said all the victims were rushed to hospital for further treatment.
Earlier, a video of the incident went viral on social media, showing a lorry believed to have been travelling against the flow of traffic before crashing into several vehicles at the road junction. — Bernama

Title: MEF welcomes RM2,000 minimum wage, says MSME exemption gives smaller firms breathing room
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) today welcomed the federal government’s decision to raise the national minimum wage to RM2,000 while exempting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales of less than RM50 million.
The new rate, effective June 2027, was announced earlier by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the tabling of Budget 2027.
MEF senior adviser for government, media and international engagement Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman said a balanced approach was essential to ensure efforts to improve workers’ welfare did not inadvertently undermine business viability, discourage hiring or put existing jobs at risk.
“Providing employers until June 2027 is a sensible step that gives businesses the time to plan, adapt and prepare for implementation while minimising disruption to employment and business operations.
“MEF believes that a reasonable transition period, combined with appropriate support for MSMEs, will help ensure that the objective of improving workers’ incomes can be pursued alongside business sustainability and job security,” he said in a statement.
Explaining further, Syed Hussain said a responsible wage policy focuses not only on the extent of wage increases but also on ensuring businesses can sustain those wages, protect existing jobs and continue creating new employment opportunities.
He also noted that while the minimum wage establishes the statutory wage floor, it should not be the ceiling for employers who can afford to pay more.
“MEF encourages employers to reward employees in line with their business performance, productivity, skills and contributions.
“At the same time, we must recognise that businesses have different financial capacities, particularly among MSMEs.
“The ultimate objective is to build sustainable businesses that can continuously create quality jobs and provide better wages for Malaysian workers,” he said.
Regarding the MSME exemption, Syed Hussain said such measures reflect an important recognition that wage policies must account for the differing financial capacities of businesses, particularly smaller enterprises that operate with tighter margins and limited resources.
“While larger businesses may have greater financial capacity to absorb higher labour costs, smaller enterprises often face more significant constraints arising from rising operating expenses, limited access to financing, productivity gaps and the challenges of adopting new technologies.
“An exemption for eligible MSMEs would provide these businesses with greater flexibility to strengthen their financial positions, improve productivity and prepare for future wage adjustments without compromising their ability to sustain employment,” he said.
Nevertheless, Syed Hussain said any exemption should be supported by clear eligibility criteria, transparent implementation guidelines and adequate communication to employers and employees.
This includes clarification on how the annual sales threshold of RM50 million will be assessed, the treatment of related companies and the application of the exemption to different business structures.
He said MEF also proposed that the federal government strengthen complementary measures to help businesses improve productivity and pay higher wages over the longer term.
These include targeted productivity incentives, support for digitalisation and automation, skills development and measures to reduce the cost of doing business, particularly for MSMEs.

Title: Haze: 36 areas record unhealthy API readings, Pasir Gudang highest at 190
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — A total of 36 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5.45pm today, with Pasir Gudang in Johor recording the highest reading at 190.
According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, other areas in Johor that recorded unhealthy API readings were Segamat (187), Larkin (185), Tangkak (183), Batu Pahat (177), Kluang (176), Pengerang (175) and Kota Tinggi (175).
In Negeri Sembilan, three areas recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Seremban (189), Nilai (183) and Port Dickson (174), while in Melaka, the affected areas were Bukit Rambai (187), Bandaraya Melaka (183) and Alor Gajah (181).
In Selangor, Johan Setia recorded the highest API reading at 181, followed by Shah Alam (175), Petaling Jaya (167), Klang (167), Banting (166) and Kuala Selangor (156).
Cheras and Batu Muda in the capital recorded readings of 177 and 172, respectively, while Putrajaya recorded 170.
Five areas in Perak also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Tasek Ipoh (182), Pegoh Ipoh (176), Tanjung Malim (174), Seri Manjung (158) and Taiping (110).
Other affected areas were Rompin (162), Indera Mahkota in Kuantan (158) and Temerloh (156) in Pahang, while in Kedah, Sungai Petani (156) and Alor Setar (152) were affected.
In addition, three areas in Penang also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Minden (154), Seberang Jaya (147) and Seberang Perai (129).
A total of 32 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while no areas recorded good readings.
API readings of zero to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are considered hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Government-owned Entities Bill to be drafted next year, RM1.1b for enforcement agencies’ operations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Enforcement agencies, including the police and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), will receive RM1.1 billion to strengthen their operations under Budget 2027.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the Finance Minister, made the announcement while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today.
The government, he said, will also draft a new Government-Owned Entities Act to strengthen good governance in government-owned companies and statutory bodies and prevent major financial scandals such as 1MDB and the mismanagement of Tabung Haji and Felda from recurring.
“With the Government Procurement Act coming to force starting 2027, the government will improve transparency and publish project details, including the contractors and contract value,” Anwar said.
“When governance is corrected, the benefits resulting from the change will contribute to the people’s welfare,” he added.
Anwar also said revenue generated from loan repayments, including from education and business loans, disbursed to federal statutory bodies must only be used for the approved purposes and target groups. This, he said, also applies to interests collected from such loans.
He also singled out the reforms that his administration has achieved since coming to power in 2022, including abolishing mandatory death penalty and penalties for suicide and enacting the Online Safety Act and the Anti-Bullying Act.
“Clearly, the hardest change is the reforms to limit one’s own powers,” he said, referring to the ongoing efforts to secure a two-thirds majority to cap a prime minister’s tenure to two terms.

Title: Budget 2027: Bumiputera contractor procurement nearly doubles to RM7.5b, GLICs to invest RM2b
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government is set to increase the procurement allocation for Bumiputera contractors in the G1 to G4 grades to RM7.5 billion under Budget 2027, an increase from RM4 billion this year.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this follows recent concerns raised by Bumiputera contractors and companies.
“For maintenance, repair and upgrading works of government facilities, the procurement threshold for direct appointment is allowed up to RM200,000 and for quotations, up to RM3 million,” he said.
He added that the Unit Peneraju Agenda Bumiputera (Teraju), a strategic agency under the Prime Minister’s Department, will provide financing of up to RM1 billion while effectively monitoring Bumiputera projects across the country.
Meanwhile, financing funds by Perbadanan Usahawan Nasional Berhad (PUNB) will increase from RM350 million previously to RM500 million.
“The government is providing a stamp duty facility of only RM10 for loan and financing agreements under the Cakna II Scheme, which will be introduced from January 1, 2027to December 31, 2030.
“The same facility will also be extended for the Cakna I Scheme until December 31, 2030,” Anwar said.
Government-linked companies (GLCs) and Petronas are targeting RM58 billion procurement from Bumiputera companies while GLC procurement guidelines — which have not been reviewed since 2006 — will be updated next year.
Anwar also announced that government-linked investment companies (GLICs) such as Ekuinas and PHB will also invest RM2 billion to further empower Bumiputera companies while Khazanah Nasional Berhad and Teraju will be introducing the RM250 million
Dana Ciptawan
(Innovators Fund) to support the growth of mid-tier Bumiputera companies.
“Centralised solar parks for government buildings will be developed with an investment of RM1.5 billion.
“This also provides opportunities for Bumiputera construction, engineering, and maintenance companies.
“Through the LSS6 solar project, 150 megawatts is allocated specifically to Bumiputera companies to support them in the clean energy industry,” Anwar said.
He added that the government is also extending the 10 Bumiputera Champions initiative with an allocation of RM40 million to foster 15 potential companies by 2027.
